description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.description:

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 15 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

entries.name: EnterPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using `find`/Glob, `grep`/Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

# ENG-2228 — Add link support to tldraw text shapes in Obsidian

## Context

Text shapes on the Obsidian tldraw canvas can't carry a link, so a simplified canvas narrative can't open the detailed source its text stands for. Geo shapes can.

**The ticket's premise is wrong, and ENG-2227 already confirmed it on the Roam side.** There is no app-side geo-link code to reuse — in `apps/obsidian` the entire link feature (the **Edit link** action, `EditLinkDialog`, the corner icon) is stock tldraw 3.14.2. Eligibility is duck-typed, not an allowlist:

```ts
// node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173 — useHasLinkShapeSelected
!!(shape && shape.type !== 'embed' && 'url' in shape.props && !shape.isLocked)
```

`TLGeoShape` declares `url`; `TLTextShape` does not. So this is a **schema change, not UI wiring**. Once `text` props carry `url`, the context-menu item and dialog light up for free — `CustomContextMenu.tsx:65` renders `<DefaultContextMenuContent />`, and there is no `actions` override anywhere in the app.

This plan mirrors the ENG-2227 Roam implementation (written, statically verified, not yet merged) so the two apps stay consistent. Roam's settled decisions carry over; the deltas are called out below.

## Decisions inherited from ENG-2227

- **Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`.** `meta` needs no migration (it's `T.jsonValue`), but it would require hand-rolling the menu item and dialog — exactly the "separate text-shape implementation" the ticket forbids.
- **A migration is mandatory, not optional.** `T.linkUrl.optional()` doesn't work: the gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is absent, so old text shapes would silently never show **Edit link**. Without the migration, `migrateStoreSnapshot` reports *success* and does nothing, then validation throws `At shape(type = text).props.url: Expected string, got undefined`.
- **Backfill defensively** (`if (props.url === undefined)`). An earlier Roam migration assigned unconditionally and clobbered user values (PR #916).
- **Replace, don't append, the default text util.** Registering both `TextShapeUtil` and a subclass throws *"defined more than once"*.
- **Vendor the hyperlink button.** tldraw does not export `HyperlinkButton` (confirmed absent from `dist-esm/index.d.mts`); mirror its markup and reuse the stock `.tl-hyperlink-button` CSS already vendored at `src/styles/style.css:1036`.

## Obsidian-specific deltas

| | Roam | Obsidian |
|---|---|---|
| Registration sites | 4 | **2** — `utils/tldraw.ts:55` and `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:109` |
| Migration home | appended v6 to `com.roam-research.discourse-graphs` | **new sequence at v1** (see below) |
| Sync worker | needed `"text"` added to `shapeType` params | **N/A** — file-based; cross-tab merge goes through `store.schema.migrateStoreSnapshot`, which applies the retroactive migration |
| Test infra | vitest exists | **none — must be stood up** |

The migration goes in a **new** sequence `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link` starting at version 1, not appended to `discourseNodeMigrations`. Roam appended because its sequence is generically named; Obsidian's existing one is `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.discourse-node`, and a text-shape migration doesn't belong there. `createMigrationSequence` only rejects sequences that don't *start* at 1, so a fresh sequence is legal. `retroactive` defaults to `true`, which is what makes it backfill files that predate it.

## Implementation

### 1. `src/components/canvas/shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (new)

Port of `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`:

```tsx
const textShapeWithLinkProps = { ...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl };

export class TextShapeWithLinkUtil extends TextShapeUtil {
  static override props = textShapeWithLinkProps;

  override getDefaultProps(): TextShapeWithLinkProps {
    return { ...super.getDefaultProps(), url: "" };
  }

  override component(shape: TLTextShape): ReturnType<TextShapeUtil["component"]> {
    const url = getTextShapeUrl(shape);
    return (<>{super.component(shape)}{url && <HyperlinkButton url={url} .../>}</>) as ...;
  }
}
```

Three things that are load-bearing:
- **`getDefaultProps` must be overridden.** `static props` alone does not add a default — the base returns an object literal, so every `createShape({type:"text"})` would fail validation on `props.url`.
- **`super.component(shape)`** rather than reimplementing the label: `useTextShapeKeydownHandler` is module-private, so a rewrite would silently drop Cmd+Enter-to-complete.
- Statics are inherited, so `static migrations = textShapeMigrations` stays untouched and keeps sequence id `com.tldraw.shape.text`. `processPropsMigrations` asserts that id for any sequence attached to the util — which is *why* the url backfill has to be a separate store-level sequence.

Roam's version reads `this.editor.getZoomLevel()` at render time rather than through `useValue`; mirror it for consistency (the hide-when-zoomed-out threshold is cosmetic).

### 2. `src/components/canvas/utils/textShapeLink.ts` (new)

Pure, dependency-free helpers, ported verbatim from `apps/roam/src/utils/textShapeLink.ts`: `isTextShapeRecord`, `hasLinkUrlProp`, `backfillTextShapeUrl`. These exist so the migration logic is unit-testable without an editor or the Obsidian API.

### 3. `src/components/canvas/shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts` (new)

Mirrors `discourseNodeMigrations.ts:36-53`: `createMigrationSequence({ sequenceId: "com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link", sequence: [{ id: versions.AddTextShapeUrl /* 1 */, scope: "record", filter: isTextShapeRecord, up: backfillTextShapeUrl, down: (s) => delete s.props.url }] })`.

### 4. `src/components/canvas/shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts` (new) + both registration sites

```ts
export const baseShapeUtils: TLAnyShapeUtilConstructor[] =
  defaultShapeUtils.map((util) => (util === TextShapeUtil ? TextShapeWithLinkUtil : util));
```

Then `...defaultShapeUtils` → `...baseShapeUtils` at **`utils/tldraw.ts:56`** and **`TldrawViewComponent.tsx:109`**, and register the migration at `utils/tldraw.ts:68` (`migrations: [discourseNodeMigrations, textLinkMigrations]`).

These two lists are consumed independently — `createTLStore` uses one for the *schema*, the `Editor` uses the other for *rendering* — and **nothing asserts they agree**. Update only the component and `updateShapes` throws on validation; update only the store and links persist but never render. That silent divergence is the reason for the shared module, same as Roam's `baseShapeUtils.ts`.

`createRawTldrawFile`'s bare `createTLStore()` at `utils/tldraw.ts:92` is left alone — it only runs with zero records, and retroactive migrations backfill on load regardless.

### 5. Test infrastructure (new for this workspace)

`apps/obsidian` has no tests at all. Mirror `apps/roam/vitest.config.mts`:

- `apps/obsidian/vitest.config.mts` — `environment: "node"`, `include: ["src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts"]`, `resolve.alias` for `~` → `src` (tsconfig paths aren't honoured automatically).
- `apps/obsidian/package.json` — add `"test": "pnpm test:unit"`, `"test:unit": "vitest run --config vitest.config.mts"`, and `"vitest": "catalog:"` to devDependencies. Per [memory: avoid `pnpm add` here], edit `package.json` by hand and run plain `pnpm install`.
- No turbo.json change: `turbo.json:78-80` already defines a generic `test:unit`, and root `ci:validate` picks it up.
- No `obsidian` module stub needed — the test imports only `tldraw` and the pure helpers. (`tldraw` imports fine headless in plain node; no jsdom.)
- `vitest` must be a real devDep because `tsconfig.json`'s `include: ["**/*.ts"]` puts the test files under `check-types`.

`src/components/canvas/utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts` ports Roam's suite: the backfill is idempotent and never overwrites a user value, non-text records are untouched, a migrated shape satisfies the `'url' in props` gate an unmigrated one fails, and — via `createTLSchema` with an extended text schema — an unmigrated text shape **throws on validation** while a migrated one round-trips its url through `migrateStoreSnapshot`. That last pair is the highest-value test: the real failure mode is `TldrawView.tsx:126-129` swallowing the throw and rendering a blank canvas.

## Known tradeoffs to surface in the PR

- **`obsidian://` page links will not work.** `T.linkUrl` accepts only `http:`/`https:`/`mailto:` (`@tldraw/validate` `validLinkProtocols`), and tldraw's `EditLinkDialog` rejects other protocols on input before the schema ever sees them. So "link to a page" — which the ticket calls the primary expected target — isn't reachable through this path. This *is* exact geo parity and matches "no new link format"; Roam shipped the same. Flag it and suggest a follow-up ticket rather than forking the dialog.
- **Forward incompatibility:** a canvas saved with a text url, opened by an *older* plugin build, fails validation and renders blank. No data loss — `onLoadFile` returns early, so the autosave listener never attaches and the file isn't overwritten. `discourseNodeMigrations` set this precedent; worth a release note.
- **Convert To drops the url.** `convertToDiscourseNode.ts` only reads `props.richText`. Correct (text→node conversion is out of scope), but say so in the PR so it isn't read as a regression.
- Worth a Linear comment to Michael that "reuse the geo-shape link code path" rested on a wrong premise, so the change isn't read as ignoring the instruction. Same note applies to ENG-2227.

## Verification

**Static** — `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian check-types`, `lint`, `test:unit`, `build`. Then grep `dist/main.js` for `AddTextShapeUrl` and `tl-hyperlink-button` to confirm the build actually contains the change. Lint: check for new *warnings* on added lines, not just errors — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings while local lint exits 0.

**In Obsidian** (the part static checks can't cover — ENG-2227 is still blocked on exactly this):
1. Text shape → right-click → Edit ▸ **Edit link** is present. Select two shapes, or lock the shape → absent.
2. Set `https://example.com` → corner icon appears; click → opens; reopen dialog → pre-filled; **Clear** → icon gone.
3. **The icon's stacking is the most likely thing to be wrong.** `.tl-text-wrapper .tl-text-content` is `pointer-events: all; z-index: var(--layer-text-content)` (`style.css:806-809`) while the button is `z-index: 1` — so for a text shape the label may cover the icon and swallow the click, in a way it doesn't for geo. Check unselected / selected / editing. If it misbehaves, the fix is one CSS rule raising the button to `--layer-text-content` (tree order then favours the later sibling, and the `--layer-text-editor` overlay still wins while editing) — **not** a wrapper div. Don't add the rule pre-emptively.
4. Double-click-to-edit still works outside the 44×44 corner.
5. **Persistence** (explicit Done When): close and reopen the canvas; then read the raw `tldraw-data` block and confirm `url` is on the text record and `schema.sequences` contains `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link: 1`.
6. **Backfill:** open a canvas file created *before* this change containing a text shape — it must load (not blank) and accept a link.
7. **Cross-tab:** same canvas in two panes; add a link in one, confirm it merges (`canvasFileSync.ts`).

Before trusting any in-app run: another worktree's dev watcher shares `~/Documents/testVault/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs`, so grep the built bundle for `AddTextShapeUrl` to confirm the vault has *this* worktree's build.

## Files

**New** — `src/components/canvas/shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts`, `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts`, `utils/textShapeLink.ts`, `utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts`, `apps/obsidian/vitest.config.mts` (all under `apps/obsidian/`).

**Modified** — `src/components/canvas/utils/tldraw.ts` (lines 56, 68), `src/components/canvas/TldrawViewComponent.tsx` (line 109), `apps/obsidian/package.json`.

**Reference** — the ENG-2227 worktree at `.claude/worktrees/eng-2227-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-roam` (uncommitted; `git diff HEAD` shows the full Roam implementation).

content.text:
No — the defensive backfill and the optional-vs-required choice are independent. Verified in `@tldraw/validate@3.14.2`:

**What `optional()` changes.** `ObjectValidator` calls `validator.validate(getOwnProperty(obj, key))`, so a missing key arrives as `undefined`, and `optional()` returns early on `undefined` (`validation.mjs:594-598`). So yes — with `T.linkUrl.optional()` an un-backfilled text shape *validates* instead of throwing `Expected string, got undefined`.

**What it doesn't change.** The defensive `if (props.url === undefined)` guards a different failure: a migration `up` running over a record that *already* has a url and clobbering it with `""`. That's what bit Roam in PR #916. Optionality has no bearing on it — you'd keep the check either way. It's one line.

**And it doesn't remove the migration.** The eligibility gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is absent. Optional-without-migration means every pre-existing text shape silently never shows **Edit link** while new ones do. So the migration is still mandatory; optional only changes what happens *if the migration doesn't run*.

So the real question is what you want that miss to look like:

- **Required** → loud: validation throws, `TldrawView.createStore` swallows it (`TldrawView.tsx:126-129`), canvas renders blank.
- **Optional** → silent: canvas opens, link UI just never appears on old shapes.

I'd keep it **required**, for three reasons. The upgrade path is already covered — the retroactive sequence runs on every load path including the cross-tab merge. The downgrade path isn't helped at all: a new file opened by an older build throws `Unexpected property` on `url` because the *old* build's validator config has no such key, regardless of how we declare it. And geo itself is `url: T.linkUrl` required, so required is literal parity — which is the ticket's framing and what ENG-2227 shipped.

What optional actually buys is turning "our migration is buggy" from a loud failure into a quiet one, and I'd rather that be loud in dev than invisible in users' vaults.

One correction to my plan either way: I wrote that `T.linkUrl.optional()` "doesn't work," which is too strong — it validates fine, it just doesn't let you skip the migration. I'll fix that line.

content.text:
Here's what actually blocks page links, and what each layer costs to change.

**Three layers say no today, not one:**

1. **The validator.** `T.linkUrl` accepts only `http:`/`https:`/`mailto:` (`validation.mjs:642`). `obsidian://open?...` is rejected by the schema.
2. **The dialog.** `EditLinkDialog.validateUrl` gates on `T.linkUrl.isValid` and otherwise retries with `https://` prepended (`EditLinkDialog.tsx:17-25`). It rejects non-web protocols *before* the schema ever sees them, so widening the validator alone changes nothing.
3. **The affordance.** `<a href target="_blank">` — fine for the web, wrong for opening a vault page in a leaf.

**What I'd been missing: this plugin already has a page-reference format, and it's better than `obsidian://`.** Discourse node shapes don't store a URL. `assetStore.ts:39-50` appends a real block to the canvas markdown —

```
[[Some Page]]
^<uuid>
```

— and stores `props.src = "asset:obsidian.blockref.<uuid>"`. `resolveLinkedTFileByBlockRef` (`assetStore.ts:77`) reads it back via `metadataCache.getFirstLinkpathDest`. Because the link is a genuine wikilink in the file, Obsidian's own machinery sees it: backlinks, graph view, and rename-following all work. An `obsidian://` string buried in our fenced JSON block gets none of that and breaks when the vault or page is renamed.

So the three real options:

| | Work | Page links |
|---|---|---|
| **Geo parity** (planned) | as planned | none |
| **`obsidian://` URLs** | widen validator + fork dialog | fragile: no backlinks, breaks on rename |
| **Block-ref wikilinks** | + action override, page picker, click branch | first-class |

The third is the one worth doing, and most of its parts exist: `overrides.actions` is a supported extension point (`TLUiOverrides.actions`, `index.d.mts:3747`), so we'd swap only `edit-link`'s `onSelect` to open our dialog while the menu item, label, icon, placement and eligibility gate stay stock; `SuggestInput.tsx`/`PublishGroupSuggestModal.tsx` give the picker; `openFileInSidebar` gives the click. We're already vendoring the button, so branching web-vs-page there is free.

Two things you should weigh before picking it. It goes past three of the ticket's explicit out-of-scope lines — page picker, new link format, and "reuse the geo-shape link code path" — so it's a re-scope, not a judgment call I should make quietly. And ENG-2227 shipped Roam as web-URL-only, so choosing this for Obsidian diverges the two apps until Roam gets an equivalent.

input.content:
# ENG-2228 — Add link support to tldraw text shapes in Obsidian

## Context

Text shapes on the Obsidian tldraw canvas can't carry a link, so a simplified canvas narrative can't open the detailed source its text stands for. Geo shapes can.

**The ticket's "reuse the geo-shape link code path" premise is wrong**, as ENG-2227 already established on the Roam side. There is no app-side geo-link code in `apps/obsidian` — the **Edit link** action, `EditLinkDialog` and the corner icon are all stock tldraw 3.14.2. Eligibility is duck-typed, not an allowlist:

```ts
// node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173 — useHasLinkShapeSelected
!!(shape && shape.type !== 'embed' && 'url' in shape.props && !shape.isLocked)
```

`TLGeoShape` declares `url`; `TLTextShape` does not. So the core of this is a **schema change**: once `text` props carry `url`, the menu item appears for free (`CustomContextMenu.tsx:65` renders `<DefaultContextMenuContent />`, and no `actions` override exists today).

**Scope decision (2026-09-14):** the ticket names page links as the primary target, so this ships `obsidian://open?vault=…&file=…` support alongside web URLs. That goes beyond strict geo parity and beyond what ENG-2227 shipped for Roam — deliberately. `obsidian://` is already this canvas's link currency: `parseObsidianOpenUrl` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:33`) and `buildObsidianUrl` (`wikilinkDragHandler.ts:14`) exist, and dropping such a URL on the canvas already creates a discourse node shape.

*Known limitation to state in the PR:* an `obsidian://` URL inside our fenced JSON block is invisible to Obsidian's link machinery — no backlinks, no graph view, and it breaks if the vault or page is renamed. The plugin's own richer pattern for this (a real `[[wikilink]]` block plus a block-ref id in `props.src`, `assetStore.ts:39-50`) survives renames. Worth a follow-up ticket; not this one.

## Decisions inherited from ENG-2227

- **Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`.** `meta` needs no migration but would require hand-rolling the menu item.
- **A migration is mandatory.** `T.linkUrl.optional()` *does* validate an absent key (`optional()` returns early on `undefined`, `validation.mjs:594-598`) — but the gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is missing, so pre-existing text shapes would silently never show **Edit link**. Optional only changes what a migration *miss* looks like.
- **`url` is required, not optional** (confirmed 2026-09-14): geo parity, and a migration miss then fails loudly rather than silently hiding the feature. Optional wouldn't help the downgrade case anyway — an older build throws `Unexpected property` on `url` regardless, since its own validator config has no such key.
- **Backfill defensively** (`if (props.url === undefined)`) — independent of the required/optional choice. An earlier Roam migration assigned unconditionally and clobbered user values (PR #916).
- **Replace, don't append, the default text util.** Registering both throws *"defined more than once"*.
- **Vendor the hyperlink button.** tldraw does not export `HyperlinkButton` (absent from `dist-esm/index.d.mts`); mirror its markup and reuse the stock `.tl-hyperlink-button` CSS already vendored at `src/styles/style.css:1036`.

## Implementation

### 1. `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (new)

Port of `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, with the validator and click handling widened:

```tsx
static override props = { ...textShapeProps, url: textLinkUrl };
override getDefaultProps() { return { ...super.getDefaultProps(), url: "" }; }
override component(shape) { return <>{super.component(shape)}{url && <HyperlinkButton .../>}</>; }
```

Load-bearing details:
- **`getDefaultProps` must be overridden.** `static props` alone gives no default — the base returns an object literal, so `createShape({type:"text"})` would fail validation on `props.url`.
- **Call `super.component(shape)`** rather than reimplementing the label: `useTextShapeKeydownHandler` is module-private, so a rewrite silently drops Cmd+Enter-to-complete.
- Statics are inherited, so `static migrations = textShapeMigrations` stays untouched at sequence id `com.tldraw.shape.text`. `processPropsMigrations` asserts that id for any sequence attached to the util — which is *why* the url backfill must be a separate store-level sequence.
- Roam's version reads `this.editor.getZoomLevel()` at render time rather than via `useValue`; mirror it (the hide-when-zoomed-out threshold is cosmetic).

### 2. `utils/textShapeLink.ts` (new)

Pure, dependency-free helpers ported from `apps/roam/src/utils/textShapeLink.ts` (`isTextShapeRecord`, `hasLinkUrlProp`, `backfillTextShapeUrl`), plus the widened validator:

```ts
const ALLOWED_PROTOCOLS = ["http:", "https:", "mailto:", "obsidian:"];
export const textLinkUrl = T.string.check(validateTextLinkUrl);
```

**This allowlist is a security boundary, not a formality** — the affordance renders `<a href={url}>`, so accepting arbitrary protocols would make `javascript:` an XSS vector. Enumerate; never fall through to "anything that parses".

Keeping these helpers free of `obsidian` imports is what makes them unit-testable without mocks.

### 3. `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts` (new)

Mirrors `discourseNodeMigrations.ts:36-53`: `createMigrationSequence({ sequenceId: "com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link", sequence: [{ id: versions.AddTextShapeUrl /* 1 */, scope: "record", filter: isTextShapeRecord, up: backfillTextShapeUrl, down: (s) => delete s.props.url }] })`.

A **new** sequence starting at v1, not appended to `discourseNodeMigrations` — Roam appended because its sequence is generically named, whereas Obsidian's is `…obsidian.discourse-node` and a text migration doesn't belong there. `createMigrationSequence` only rejects sequences that don't *start* at 1. `retroactive` defaults to `true`, which is what backfills files predating it.

### 4. `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts` (new) + both registration sites

```ts
export const baseShapeUtils = defaultShapeUtils.map((u) =>
  u === TextShapeUtil ? TextShapeWithLinkUtil : u);
```

Swap `...defaultShapeUtils` → `...baseShapeUtils` at **`utils/tldraw.ts:56`** and **`TldrawViewComponent.tsx:109`**, and register the migration at `utils/tldraw.ts:68`.

These two lists are consumed independently — `createTLStore` for the *schema*, the `Editor` for *rendering* — and **nothing asserts they agree**. Update only the component and `updateShapes` throws; update only the store and links persist but never render. Hence the shared module, as in Roam's `baseShapeUtils.ts`.

`createRawTldrawFile`'s bare `createTLStore()` at `utils/tldraw.ts:92` is left alone — zero records, and retroactive migrations backfill on load anyway.

### 5. `TextLinkDialog.tsx` (new) + an `edit-link` action override

tldraw's dialog gates on `T.linkUrl.isValid` and retries with `https://` prepended (`EditLinkDialog.tsx:17-25`), so it rejects `obsidian://` *before* the schema sees it. Widening the validator alone accomplishes nothing — the dialog must be forked.

`EditLinkDialog` itself is not exported, but every primitive it uses is (`TldrawUiDialogBody/Header/Footer/Title/CloseButton`, `TldrawUiInput`, `TldrawUiButton`, `TldrawUiButtonLabel`), so the fork is a faithful, visually identical copy with `validateUrl` swapped.

Swap it in via the supported `TLUiOverrides.actions` hook (`index.d.mts:3747`), extending the existing `overrides` object at `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:466` (currently `tools` only). Replace only `edit-link`'s `onSelect` — `helpers.addDialog({ component: TextLinkDialog })`, preceded by `editor.markHistoryStoppingPoint("edit-link")` as the stock action does (`actions.tsx:153-160`). Label, icon, placement and the eligibility gate all stay stock.

**The trap:** this override is global, so the forked dialog also serves *geo* shapes — whose `url` prop is still stock `T.linkUrl`. Letting an `obsidian://` URL through for a geo shape would throw at `editor.updateShapes`. The dialog must therefore pick its validator from the selected shape's type (wide for `text`, stock `T.linkUrl` otherwise). Cover this with a test; it is the most likely silent regression in the change.

### 6. Click handling in the vendored button

Branch on protocol. Web/mailto → plain `<a href target="_blank">`, exactly as geo. `obsidian:` → `preventDefault`, then `parseObsidianOpenUrl` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:33`) → resolve to a `TFile` → `openFileInSidebar` (`openFileUtils.ts:68`). Handling it in-app avoids an OS protocol round trip that would defocus and re-enter Obsidian.

`resolveObsidianUrlToFile` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:56`) already does the vault-name check and the `.md` suffix retry — export it rather than writing a second copy. Show a `Notice` when the target is another vault or missing (per house style, `Notice`, not `console.*`).

### 7. Test infrastructure (new for this workspace)

`apps/obsidian` has no tests at all. Mirror `apps/roam/vitest.config.mts`:

- `apps/obsidian/vitest.config.mts` — `environment: "node"`, `include: ["src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts"]`, `resolve.alias` `~` → `src` (tsconfig paths aren't honoured automatically).
- `apps/obsidian/package.json` — add `"test": "pnpm test:unit"`, `"test:unit": "vitest run --config vitest.config.mts"`, and `"vitest": "catalog:"`. Per [memory] edit `package.json` by hand and run plain `pnpm install`, not `pnpm add`, to keep the lockfile diff small.
- No `turbo.json` change — `turbo.json:78-80` already defines a generic `test:unit`, which root `ci:validate` picks up.
- `vitest` must be a real devDep: `tsconfig.json`'s `include: ["**/*.ts"]` puts test files under `check-types`.
- No `obsidian` module stub needed if tests import only `tldraw` and the pure helpers. (`tldraw` imports fine headless; no jsdom.)

`utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts` ports Roam's suite plus the new validator cases:
- backfill is idempotent, never overwrites a user value, leaves non-text records alone;
- a migrated shape satisfies the `'url' in props` gate an unmigrated one fails;
- via `createTLSchema` with an extended text schema, an unmigrated text shape **throws on validation** while a migrated one round-trips its url through `migrateStoreSnapshot` — the highest-value test, since the real failure mode is `TldrawView.tsx:126-129` swallowing the throw into a blank canvas;
- `textLinkUrl` accepts http/https/mailto/`obsidian://open?…` and **rejects `javascript:`**, `file:`, and unparseable junk;
- the dialog picks the wide validator for `text` and the stock one for `geo`.

## Verification

**Static** — `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian check-types`, `lint`, `test:unit`, `build`; then grep `dist/main.js` for `AddTextShapeUrl` and `tl-hyperlink-button` to confirm the build contains the change. Check for new lint *warnings* on added lines, not just errors — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings while local lint exits 0.

**In Obsidian:**
1. Text shape → right-click → Edit ▸ **Edit link** present. Two shapes selected, or shape locked → absent.
2. `https://example.com` → icon appears; click opens; reopening the dialog pre-fills; **Clear** removes it.
3. **Page link:** copy a page's Obsidian URL, paste it in, confirm the dialog *accepts* it (this is what the fork exists for) and clicking opens that page in the sidebar without the window defocusing.
4. **Geo regression:** a geo shape still takes a web URL, and an `obsidian://` URL on a geo shape is rejected by the dialog rather than throwing.
5. **Icon stacking is the likeliest visual bug.** `.tl-text-wrapper .tl-text-content` is `pointer-events: all; z-index: var(--layer-text-content)` (`style.css:806-809`) while the button is `z-index: 1`, so a text shape's label may cover the icon and swallow the click in a way it doesn't for geo. Check unselected / selected / editing. If it misbehaves, the fix is one CSS rule raising the button to `--layer-text-content` (tree order then favours the later sibling, and `--layer-text-editor` still wins while editing) — **not** a wrapper div. Don't add it pre-emptively.
6. Double-click-to-edit still works outside the 44×44 corner.
7. **Persistence** (explicit Done When): close and reopen the canvas; read the raw `tldraw-data` block and confirm `url` is on the text record and `schema.sequences` contains `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link: 1`.
8. **Backfill:** open a canvas created *before* this change containing a text shape — it must load (not blank) and accept a link.
9. **Cross-tab:** same canvas in two panes; add a link in one, confirm it merges (`canvasFileSync.ts`).

Before trusting any in-app run: another worktree's dev watcher shares `~/Documents/testVault/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs`, so grep the built bundle for `AddTextShapeUrl` to confirm the vault has *this* worktree's build.

## PR notes

- Say that "reuse the geo-shape link code path" rested on a wrong premise (no such app-side code exists) so the change isn't read as ignoring the instruction — same note applies to ENG-2227. Worth a Linear comment to Michael.
- Flag the divergence from ENG-2227: Obsidian accepts `obsidian://`, Roam is web-only.
- Flag the rename/backlink limitation of `obsidian://` and propose the block-ref follow-up.
- **Forward incompatibility:** a canvas saved with a text url, opened by an *older* plugin build, fails validation and renders blank. No data loss — `onLoadFile` returns early so the autosave listener never attaches and the file isn't overwritten. `discourseNodeMigrations` set this precedent; worth a release note.

# ENG-2228 — Add link support to tldraw text shapes in Obsidian

## Context

Text shapes on the Obsidian tldraw canvas can't carry a link, so a simplified canvas narrative can't open the detailed source its text stands for. Geo shapes can.

**The ticket's "reuse the geo-shape link code path" premise is wrong**, as ENG-2227 already established on the Roam side. There is no app-side geo-link code in `apps/obsidian` — the **Edit link** action, `EditLinkDialog` and the corner icon are all stock tldraw 3.14.2. Eligibility is duck-typed, not an allowlist:

```ts
// node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173 — useHasLinkShapeSelected
!!(shape && shape.type !== 'embed' && 'url' in shape.props && !shape.isLocked)
```

`TLGeoShape` declares `url`; `TLTextShape` does not. So the core of this is a **schema change**: once `text` props carry `url`, the menu item appears for free (`CustomContextMenu.tsx:65` renders `<DefaultContextMenuContent />`, and no `actions` override exists today).

**Scope decision (2026-09-14):** the ticket names page links as the primary target, so this ships `obsidian://open?vault=…&file=…` support alongside web URLs. That goes beyond strict geo parity and beyond what ENG-2227 shipped for Roam — deliberately. `obsidian://` is already this canvas's link currency: `parseObsidianOpenUrl` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:33`) and `buildObsidianUrl` (`wikilinkDragHandler.ts:14`) exist, and dropping such a URL on the canvas already creates a discourse node shape.

*Known limitation to state in the PR:* an `obsidian://` URL inside our fenced JSON block is invisible to Obsidian's link machinery — no backlinks, no graph view, and it breaks if the vault or page is renamed. The plugin's own richer pattern for this (a real `[[wikilink]]` block plus a block-ref id in `props.src`, `assetStore.ts:39-50`) survives renames. Worth a follow-up ticket; not this one.

## Decisions inherited from ENG-2227

- **Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`.** `meta` needs no migration but would require hand-rolling the menu item.
- **A migration is mandatory.** `T.linkUrl.optional()` *does* validate an absent key (`optional()` returns early on `undefined`, `validation.mjs:594-598`) — but the gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is missing, so pre-existing text shapes would silently never show **Edit link**. Optional only changes what a migration *miss* looks like.
- **`url` is required, not optional** (confirmed 2026-09-14): geo parity, and a migration miss then fails loudly rather than silently hiding the feature. Optional wouldn't help the downgrade case anyway — an older build throws `Unexpected property` on `url` regardless, since its own validator config has no such key.
- **Backfill defensively** (`if (props.url === undefined)`) — independent of the required/optional choice. An earlier Roam migration assigned unconditionally and clobbered user values (PR #916).
- **Replace, don't append, the default text util.** Registering both throws *"defined more than once"*.
- **Vendor the hyperlink button.** tldraw does not export `HyperlinkButton` (absent from `dist-esm/index.d.mts`); mirror its markup and reuse the stock `.tl-hyperlink-button` CSS already vendored at `src/styles/style.css:1036`.

## Implementation

### 1. `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (new)

Port of `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, with the validator and click handling widened:

```tsx
static override props = { ...textShapeProps, url: textLinkUrl };
override getDefaultProps() { return { ...super.getDefaultProps(), url: "" }; }
override component(shape) { return <>{super.component(shape)}{url && <HyperlinkButton .../>}</>; }
```

Load-bearing details:
- **`getDefaultProps` must be overridden.** `static props` alone gives no default — the base returns an object literal, so `createShape({type:"text"})` would fail validation on `props.url`.
- **Call `super.component(shape)`** rather than reimplementing the label: `useTextShapeKeydownHandler` is module-private, so a rewrite silently drops Cmd+Enter-to-complete.
- Statics are inherited, so `static migrations = textShapeMigrations` stays untouched at sequence id `com.tldraw.shape.text`. `processPropsMigrations` asserts that id for any sequence attached to the util — which is *why* the url backfill must be a separate store-level sequence.
- Roam's version reads `this.editor.getZoomLevel()` at render time rather than via `useValue`; mirror it (the hide-when-zoomed-out threshold is cosmetic).

### 2. `utils/textShapeLink.ts` (new)

Pure, dependency-free helpers ported from `apps/roam/src/utils/textShapeLink.ts` (`isTextShapeRecord`, `hasLinkUrlProp`, `backfillTextShapeUrl`), plus the widened validator:

```ts
const ALLOWED_PROTOCOLS = ["http:", "https:", "mailto:", "obsidian:"];
export const textLinkUrl = T.string.check(validateTextLinkUrl);
```

**This allowlist is a security boundary, not a formality** — the affordance renders `<a href={url}>`, so accepting arbitrary protocols would make `javascript:` an XSS vector. Enumerate; never fall through to "anything that parses".

Keeping these helpers free of `obsidian` imports is what makes them unit-testable without mocks.

### 3. `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts` (new)

Mirrors `discourseNodeMigrations.ts:36-53`: `createMigrationSequence({ sequenceId: "com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link", sequence: [{ id: versions.AddTextShapeUrl /* 1 */, scope: "record", filter: isTextShapeRecord, up: backfillTextShapeUrl, down: (s) => delete s.props.url }] })`.

A **new** sequence starting at v1, not appended to `discourseNodeMigrations` — Roam appended because its sequence is generically named, whereas Obsidian's is `…obsidian.discourse-node` and a text migration doesn't belong there. `createMigrationSequence` only rejects sequences that don't *start* at 1. `retroactive` defaults to `true`, which is what backfills files predating it.

### 4. `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts` (new) + both registration sites

```ts
export const baseShapeUtils = defaultShapeUtils.map((u) =>
  u === TextShapeUtil ? TextShapeWithLinkUtil : u);
```

Swap `...defaultShapeUtils` → `...baseShapeUtils` at **`utils/tldraw.ts:56`** and **`TldrawViewComponent.tsx:109`**, and register the migration at `utils/tldraw.ts:68`.

These two lists are consumed independently — `createTLStore` for the *schema*, the `Editor` for *rendering* — and **nothing asserts they agree**. Update only the component and `updateShapes` throws; update only the store and links persist but never render. Hence the shared module, as in Roam's `baseShapeUtils.ts`.

`createRawTldrawFile`'s bare `createTLStore()` at `utils/tldraw.ts:92` is left alone — zero records, and retroactive migrations backfill on load anyway.

### 5. `TextLinkDialog.tsx` (new) + an `edit-link` action override

tldraw's dialog gates on `T.linkUrl.isValid` and retries with `https://` prepended (`EditLinkDialog.tsx:17-25`), so it rejects `obsidian://` *before* the schema sees it. Widening the validator alone accomplishes nothing — the dialog must be forked.

`EditLinkDialog` itself is not exported, but every primitive it uses is (`TldrawUiDialogBody/Header/Footer/Title/CloseButton`, `TldrawUiInput`, `TldrawUiButton`, `TldrawUiButtonLabel`), so the fork is a faithful, visually identical copy with `validateUrl` swapped.

Swap it in via the supported `TLUiOverrides.actions` hook (`index.d.mts:3747`), extending the existing `overrides` object at `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:466` (currently `tools` only). Replace only `edit-link`'s `onSelect` — `helpers.addDialog({ component: TextLinkDialog })`, preceded by `editor.markHistoryStoppingPoint("edit-link")` as the stock action does (`actions.tsx:153-160`). Label, icon, placement and the eligibility gate all stay stock.

**The trap:** this override is global, so the forked dialog also serves *geo* shapes — whose `url` prop is still stock `T.linkUrl`. Letting an `obsidian://` URL through for a geo shape would throw at `editor.updateShapes`. The dialog must therefore pick its validator from the selected shape's type (wide for `text`, stock `T.linkUrl` otherwise). Cover this with a test; it is the most likely silent regression in the change.

### 6. Click handling in the vendored button

Branch on protocol. Web/mailto → plain `<a href target="_blank">`, exactly as geo. `obsidian:` → `preventDefault`, then `parseObsidianOpenUrl` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:33`) → resolve to a `TFile` → `openFileInSidebar` (`openFileUtils.ts:68`). Handling it in-app avoids an OS protocol round trip that would defocus and re-enter Obsidian.

`resolveObsidianUrlToFile` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:56`) already does the vault-name check and the `.md` suffix retry — export it rather than writing a second copy. Show a `Notice` when the target is another vault or missing (per house style, `Notice`, not `console.*`).

### 7. Test infrastructure (new for this workspace)

`apps/obsidian` has no tests at all. Mirror `apps/roam/vitest.config.mts`:

- `apps/obsidian/vitest.config.mts` — `environment: "node"`, `include: ["src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts"]`, `resolve.alias` `~` → `src` (tsconfig paths aren't honoured automatically).
- `apps/obsidian/package.json` — add `"test": "pnpm test:unit"`, `"test:unit": "vitest run --config vitest.config.mts"`, and `"vitest": "catalog:"`. Per [memory] edit `package.json` by hand and run plain `pnpm install`, not `pnpm add`, to keep the lockfile diff small.
- No `turbo.json` change — `turbo.json:78-80` already defines a generic `test:unit`, which root `ci:validate` picks up.
- `vitest` must be a real devDep: `tsconfig.json`'s `include: ["**/*.ts"]` puts test files under `check-types`.
- No `obsidian` module stub needed if tests import only `tldraw` and the pure helpers. (`tldraw` imports fine headless; no jsdom.)

`utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts` ports Roam's suite plus the new validator cases:
- backfill is idempotent, never overwrites a user value, leaves non-text records alone;
- a migrated shape satisfies the `'url' in props` gate an unmigrated one fails;
- via `createTLSchema` with an extended text schema, an unmigrated text shape **throws on validation** while a migrated one round-trips its url through `migrateStoreSnapshot` — the highest-value test, since the real failure mode is `TldrawView.tsx:126-129` swallowing the throw into a blank canvas;
- `textLinkUrl` accepts http/https/mailto/`obsidian://open?…` and **rejects `javascript:`**, `file:`, and unparseable junk;
- the dialog picks the wide validator for `text` and the stock one for `geo`.

## Verification

**Static** — `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian check-types`, `lint`, `test:unit`, `build`; then grep `dist/main.js` for `AddTextShapeUrl` and `tl-hyperlink-button` to confirm the build contains the change. Check for new lint *warnings* on added lines, not just errors — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings while local lint exits 0.

**In Obsidian:**
1. Text shape → right-click → Edit ▸ **Edit link** present. Two shapes selected, or shape locked → absent.
2. `https://example.com` → icon appears; click opens; reopening the dialog pre-fills; **Clear** removes it.
3. **Page link:** copy a page's Obsidian URL, paste it in, confirm the dialog *accepts* it (this is what the fork exists for) and clicking opens that page in the sidebar without the window defocusing.
4. **Geo regression:** a geo shape still takes a web URL, and an `obsidian://` URL on a geo shape is rejected by the dialog rather than throwing.
5. **Icon stacking is the likeliest visual bug.** `.tl-text-wrapper .tl-text-content` is `pointer-events: all; z-index: var(--layer-text-content)` (`style.css:806-809`) while the button is `z-index: 1`, so a text shape's label may cover the icon and swallow the click in a way it doesn't for geo. Check unselected / selected / editing. If it misbehaves, the fix is one CSS rule raising the button to `--layer-text-content` (tree order then favours the later sibling, and `--layer-text-editor` still wins while editing) — **not** a wrapper div. Don't add it pre-emptively.
6. Double-click-to-edit still works outside the 44×44 corner.
7. **Persistence** (explicit Done When): close and reopen the canvas; read the raw `tldraw-data` block and confirm `url` is on the text record and `schema.sequences` contains `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link: 1`.
8. **Backfill:** open a canvas created *before* this change containing a text shape — it must load (not blank) and accept a link.
9. **Cross-tab:** same canvas in two panes; add a link in one, confirm it merges (`canvasFileSync.ts`).

Before trusting any in-app run: another worktree's dev watcher shares `~/Documents/testVault/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs`, so grep the built bundle for `AddTextShapeUrl` to confirm the vault has *this* worktree's build.

## PR notes

- Say that "reuse the geo-shape link code path" rested on a wrong premise (no such app-side code exists) so the change isn't read as ignoring the instruction — same note applies to ENG-2227. Worth a Linear comment to Michael.
- Flag the divergence from ENG-2227: Obsidian accepts `obsidian://`, Roam is web-only.
- Flag the rename/backlink limitation of `obsidian://` and propose the block-ref follow-up.
- **Forward incompatibility:** a canvas saved with a text url, opened by an *older* plugin build, fails validation and renders blank. No data loss — `onLoadFile` returns early so the autosave listener never attaches and the file isn't overwritten. `discourseNodeMigrations` set this precedent; worth a release note.
- **Convert To drops the url** (`convertToDiscourseNode.ts` reads only `props.richText`). Correct, since text→node conversion is out of scope, but say so explicitly.

*Known limitation to state in the PR:* an `obsidian://` URL inside our fenced JSON block is invisible to Obsidian's link machinery — no backlinks, no graph view, and it breaks if the vault or page is renamed. The plugin's own richer pattern for this (a real `[[wikilink]]` block plus a block-ref id in `props.src`, `assetStore.ts:39-50`) survives renames. Worth a follow-up ticket; not this one.

## Decisions inherited from ENG-2227

- **Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`.** `meta` needs no migration but would require hand-rolling the menu item.
- **A migration is mandatory.** `T.linkUrl.optional()` *does* validate an absent key (`optional()` returns early on `undefined`, `validation.mjs:594-598`) — but the gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is missing, so pre-existing text shapes would silently never show **Edit link**. - **`url` is required, not optional** (confirmed 2026-09-14): geo parity, and a migration miss then fails loudly rather than silently hiding the feature. - **Backfill defensively** (`if (props.url === undefined)`) — independent of the required/optional choice. An earlier Roam migration assigned unconditionally and clobbered user values (PR #916).

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Style Guide

### UI Guidelines

- Use Tailwind CSS for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use tailwind classes
- Use platform-native UI components (see below) first with shadcn/ui as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles
- Use `text-red-700` for Roam error message text. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`. This convention does not change danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, or diagram colors.

### TypeScript Guidelines

- Prefer `type` over `interface`
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Avoid `any` types when possible
- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

### Code Formatting

- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
  - PascalCase for components and types
  - camelCase for variables and functions
  - UPPERCASE for constants

### Code Organization

- Prefer small, focused functions over inline code
- Extract complex logic into well-named functions
- Function names should describe their purpose clearly
- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary
- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions
- Prefer early returns over nested conditionals for better readability
- Prefer util functions for reusable logic and common operations

### Documentation

- Add comments only when necessary; descriptive names should minimize the need for comments
- Explain the why, not the what, focusing on reasoning, trade-offs, and approaches
- Document limitations, known bugs, or edge cases where behavior may not align with expectations
- Prefer sentence case in documentation and feature descriptions; capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase to emphasize user actions

### Testing

- Write unit tests for new functionality
- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them
- Before opening a pull request or declaring work PR-ready, run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` followed by `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root, and resolve any failures
- After opening or updating an authorized pull request, wait for its required GitHub checks and report their final status
