Keep the app-level `TextShapeWithLinkUtil` subclass; **do not** pursue (c). Total: 2 packages, 5 files, no schema change — comparable in size to the `tldraw@2.4.6` patch already in the tree.   ---
  
  ## 1. Does `meta` avoid a migration? — YES, unambiguously
  
  `meta` is typed `JsonObject` on the base shape and validated permissively:
  
  `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-2228-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-obsidian/node_modules/.pnpm/@tldraw+tlschema@3.14.2_react-dom@18.2.0_react@18.2.0__react@18.2.0/node_modules/@tldraw/tlschema/src/shapes/TLBaseShape.ts:20` — `meta: JsonObject`
  Same file `:55-56` — the validator body:
  ```
  props: props ? T.object(props) : (T.jsonValue as any),
  meta:  meta  ? T.object(meta)  : (T.jsonValue as any),
  ```
  
  And the critical bit: **a shape util can never supply a `meta` validator.** `utilsToMap` in
  `/…/@tldraw+editor@3.14.2…/node_modules/@tldraw/editor/src/lib/config/createTLStore.ts:140-150` forwards only `props` and `migrations` to `SchemaPropsInfo`; `meta` is dropped on the floor. So for every shape type in this app, `createShapeValidator` is called with `meta === undefined` → `meta` is validated as `T.jsonValue`, i.e. "any JSON". (`SchemaPropsInfo` declares an optional `meta` field at `…/tlschema/src/createTLSchema.ts:43-47`, but nothing in the editor's util pipeline populates it.)
  
  Contrast with `props`: `T.object` throws on unknown keys —
  `/…/@tldraw+validate@3.14.2/node_modules/@tldraw/validate/src/lib/validation.ts:299-303` and `:335-341`, `throw new ValidationError('Unexpected property', [key])`. That is exactly why the current branch needs `textLinkMigrations.ts`.
  
  Absence needs no backfill either: the shape record type defaults `meta: {}`
  (`…/tlschema/src/records/TLShape.ts` → `createShapeRecordType`, `withDefaultProperties(() => ({ …, meta: {} }))`, lines ~206-213), and `Editor.createShapes` merges `{...this.getInitialMetaForShape(shape), ...shape.meta}` (`…/editor/src/lib/editor/Editor.ts:7966-7969`), so there is no `getDefaultProps` analogue to override.
  
  **Verdict: with `meta`, existing canvas files load completely untouched — no migration sequence, no `schemaBeforeAppMigrations` fallback, no schema change.** `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts` (31 lines) and the `schemaBeforeAppMigrations` plumbing added to `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/tldraw.ts` (+~20) and `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/canvasFileSync.ts` (+6) all disappear. The reviewer is right on this point.
  
  ---
  
  ## 2. What stops working — all stock link UI is props-gated
  
  ### `useHasLinkShapeSelected`
  `apps/obsidian/node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173-188`:
  ```ts
  const onlySelectedShape = editor.getOnlySelectedShape()
  return !!(
    onlySelectedShape &&
    onlySelectedShape.type !== 'embed' &&
    'url' in onlySelectedShape.props &&
    !onlySelectedShape.isLocked
  )
  ```
  Hard-coded `'url' in …props`. Not overridable, not parameterised. With `meta.url` this returns `false` for text shapes forever. **We would have to write our own `useHasTextLinkSelected` hook (~12 lines with `useValue`).**
  
  ### `EditLinkMenuItem` and its three render sites
  - `apps/obsidian/node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/menu-items.tsx:43-48` — `if (!useHasLinkShapeSelected()) return null`.
  - Rendered inside `EditMenuSubmenu` at `menu-items.tsx:360`, which `DefaultContextMenuContent` renders at `apps/obsidian/node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/ContextMenu/DefaultContextMenuContent.tsx:35`.
  - Also `…/MainMenu/DefaultMainMenuContent.tsx:91` and a second, independent copy in `…/ActionsMenu/DefaultActionsMenuContent.tsx:128-134`.
  
  Today `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/CustomContextMenu.tsx:64` renders `<DefaultContextMenuContent />`, so with `props.url` **all three entry points light up for text shapes for free, in tldraw's own position inside the Edit submenu.** With `meta.url` we get **zero** of them and must hand-build a menu item. Inserting it at the same position inside `EditMenuSubmenu` is not possible without forking `DefaultContextMenuContent` (~60 lines); the cheap option is a separate `TldrawUiMenuGroup` in `CustomContextMenu.tsx` (~30 lines) — which puts "Edit link" in a different place for text than for geo/bookmark shapes. There is no keyboard shortcut fallback: the `edit-link` action has no `kbd`.
  
  ### `EditLinkDialog`
  `apps/obsidian/node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/EditLinkDialog.tsx:35-39` guard (`'url' in selectedShape.props`), `:57` / `:60` reads `selectedShape.props.url`, and both writes go through props — `:101-103` (`props: { url: '' }`) and `:116-122` (`props: { url: urlInputState.safe }`).
  
  **Important: this dialog is already unusable for us under either approach.** It validates with `T.linkUrl`, whose protocol allowlist is `http:/https:/mailto:` only (`…/@tldraw+validate@3.14.2/…/src/lib/validation.ts:958-974`), so `obsidian://open?...` is rejected and rewritten to `https://`. The fork at `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/TextLinkDialog.tsx` exists because of the `obsidian://` requirement, **not** because of props-vs-meta. Under `meta` the same 214-line fork is needed, with two lines changed (`props: {url}` → `meta: {url}`). Note `editor.updateShapes` supports partial `meta` merges identically to props — `applyPartialToRecordWithProps`, `…/editor/src/lib/editor/Editor.ts:10685-10691` (`if (k === 'props' || k === 'meta')`).

  `apps/obsidian/node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/context/actions.tsx:149-161`. The action itself is shape-agnostic — it only does guards + `markHistoryStoppingPoint` + `addDialog`. Under `meta` we would not patch it at all; we'd call `addDialog({component: TextLinkDialog})` from our own menu item and reimplement the two guards (`canApplySelectionAction`, `mustGoBackToSelectToolFirst`) — roughly a wash with the current 22-line `actions` override in `TldrawViewComponent.tsx`.
  
  ### One thing `meta` does NOT break
  `meta` changes do re-render the shape. `InnerShape`'s memo comparator is `areShapesContentEqual` (`…/editor/src/lib/components/Shape.tsx:194`) = `a.props === b.props && a.meta === b.meta` (`…/editor/src/lib/utils/areShapesContentEqual.ts:3-4`); `InnerShapeBackground` compares both explicitly at `Shape.tsx:214-217`; the comment at `Shape.tsx:188-190` says "even if the props/meta have not changed".   ---
  
  ## 3. Net custom-code comparison
  
  Current branch: 11 files, **523 insertions** (`git diff --stat 47605145..HEAD -- apps/obsidian`).
  
  | Piece | props (current) | meta |
  |---|---|---|
  | `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` | 121 (incl. vendored `HyperlinkButton`, `static props`, `getDefaultProps`) | **still needed**, ~115 (drop `static props`+`getDefaultProps`, read `shape.meta.url`) |
  | `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts` | 21 (must swap `TextShapeUtil`) | **still needed**, 21 — the util is what renders the icon |
  | `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts` | 31 | **0 — deleted** |
  | `utils/tldraw.ts` `schemaBeforeAppMigrations` + `APP_MIGRATIONS` | ~+20 | **0** |
  | `utils/canvasFileSync.ts` schema fallback | +6 | **0** |
  | `utils/textShapeLink.ts` | 53 (`textLinkUrl` T-validator, `isTextShapeRecord`, `backfillTextShapeUrl`) | ~30 — keep `isAllowedTextLinkUrl`; the T-validator has nothing to attach to |
  | `TextLinkDialog.tsx` fork | 214 | **214, unchanged** (needed for `obsidian://` either way) |
  | `TldrawViewComponent.tsx` `actions` override | +22 | ~+12 (dialog opened from own menu item) |
  | custom menu item + gate hook | **0 — stock `EditLinkMenuItem` reused in 3 places** | **+~40 new** (`useHasTextLinkSelected` + `TldrawUiMenuGroup`/`TldrawUiMenuItem` in `CustomContextMenu.tsx`) |
  | render-time URL sanitisation | 0 (schema rejects bad URLs at load) | **+~8 new** — see below |
  | `icons.ts`, `styles.css` | +17 | +17 |
  | **files touched** | **11** | **~8** |
  | **rough total** | **~523** | **~460** |

  - "avoids backfilling / keeps the props schema" — **correct and valuable**.
  - "reuses the stock UI / less custom code to maintain" — **backwards on reuse.** The props approach's whole point is that `'url' in props` is tldraw's own feature detection; paying the migration buys three stock menu entries, the eligibility gate, the icon, the label and the placement. Moving to `meta` makes us the owner of all of that. The line count still nets out slightly in meta's favour only because the migration + schema-fallback plumbing is bulky.
  - A custom shape util is required either way.
  
  **New risk `meta` introduces:** `meta` is `T.jsonValue`, so nothing validates it. The `textLinkUrl` allowlist in `utils/textShapeLink.ts:32-38` — which exists to stop `javascript:` becoming an XSS vector via the rendered `<a href>` — currently runs at schema level and rejects a malicious value at file-load time. Under `meta` it can only run in the dialog (write path) and must be re-applied defensively in `HyperlinkButton` before setting `href`, because a hand-edited or third-party-authored `.md` canvas can put anything in `meta.url` and it will load cleanly. That is a genuine security-posture regression unless the render-time guard is added.
  
  ---
  
  ## 4. Other consequences of `meta`
  
  - **Copy/paste:** preserved. `getContentFromCurrentPage` pushes whole shape records (`Editor.ts:8977-8983`, `{...shape, x, y, rotation, parentId}`); `putContentOntoCurrentPage` rebuilds with `const newShape = { ...oldShape, id: newId }` (`Editor.ts:9200`) and calls `createShapes` (`:9303`), which merges `{...getInitialMetaForShape(shape), ...shape.meta}` — existing meta wins (`Editor.ts:7966-7969`).
  - **Duplicate:** preserved — `duplicateShapes` spreads the original shape (`Editor.ts:6272-6281`).
  - **Undo/redo:** preserved. `updateShapes` → `applyPartialToRecordWithProps` produces a new record object (`Editor.ts:10665-10698`) and the store diffs whole records; `meta` is not special-cased anywhere in history.
  - **App save path:** preserved. `createRawTldrawFile` (`apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/tldraw.ts:108-115`) serialises `store.allRecords()` verbatim — full records, meta included.
  - **`convertToDiscourseNode`:** **drops the link under both approaches.** `createDiscourseNodeShape` builds a brand-new `discourse-node` shape with a fresh `props` object and no `meta`, then deletes the source shape — `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/convertToDiscourseNode.ts:239-255` (`editor.createShape({... props: {w,h,src,title,nodeTypeId,imageSrc}})` then `editor.deleteShape(shape.id)`). Neither `props.url` nor `meta.url` is carried over. No differentiator; pre-existing gap either way.
  - **Precedent in apps/obsidian:** yes, `shape.meta` is already the app's chosen place for out-of-band shape data:
    - `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/shapes/DiscourseRelationShape.tsx:1147-1148` — `meta: { ...shape.meta, … }`
    - `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/shapes/DiscourseRelationBinding.tsx:165` — `if (arrow.meta.relationInstanceId) return`
    - `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/overlays/RelationPanel.tsx:474` — `meta: { ...shape.meta, relationInstanceId }`
    - `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/convertArrowToDiscourseRelation.ts:237-238`
    (`apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/TldrawView.tsx:109` is file-level `TLData.meta`, not shape meta — different thing.)
    So `relationInstanceId` is an exact existing precedent for "app-specific value on an otherwise-stock shape, stored in meta, no migration".
  
  ---
  
  ## 5. Forward/backward compatibility — `meta` wins clearly
  
  Unknown migration sequences in a persisted schema are **silently ignored**, not migrated down: `StoreSchema.getMigrationsSince` starts from `Object.keys(schema.sequences).filter(id => this.migrations[id])` — `/…/@tldraw+store@3.14.2_react@18.2.0/node_modules/@tldraw/store/src/lib/StoreSchema.ts:162-178`.
  
  - **props approach:** a file written by the new build carries `props.url` on every text shape *and* `sequences["com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link"] = 1`. An older plugin build has no such sequence → the filter drops it → no down-migration runs → records keep `props.url` → the stock `TextShapeUtil`'s `T.object(textShapeProps)` throws `Unexpected property: url` (`validation.ts:299-303`) → store load fails → blank canvas. Confirmed as described.
  - **meta approach:** no new sequence is written at all, and `meta` validates as `T.jsonValue`. An older build loads the file fine, ignores `meta.url` (no icon rendered), and — because `createRawTldrawFile` round-trips `store.allRecords()` — **writes `meta.url` back out intact on save.** Lossless forward/backward round-trip.
  
  This is the strongest argument for `meta`, and it is stronger than the line-count argument.
  
  ---
  
  ## Bottom line
  
  **Recommend `shape.meta.url`, but not for the reason given.**
  
  The reviewer is right that `meta` removes the migration and the schema-fallback plumbing (`meta` is `T.jsonValue` because `utilsToMap` never forwards a meta validator), and right that existing files load untouched. The reviewer is **wrong that it reduces custom code by reusing more of tldraw** — it is the opposite: `props.url` is the key that unlocks tldraw's stock link UI (`useHasLinkShapeSelected` → `EditLinkMenuItem` in context menu, main menu and actions menu), and `meta` forfeits all of it, forcing a hand-built menu item and gate hook. Net is only ~60-70 lines lighter, and a custom shape util plus the 214-line dialog fork are required either way.
  
  The decisive trade is compatibility, not code volume:
  - **Choose `meta` if** cross-version file compatibility matters — an older build opening a new file renders normally and round-trips the link, versus the props approach bricking the canvas. Cost: build and own the menu item (~40 lines), accept non-stock menu placement for text shapes, and **add a render-time `isAllowedTextLinkUrl` guard in `HyperlinkButton`**, since nothing validates `meta` at load and `javascript:` would otherwise reach the `<a href>`.
  - **Choose `props` if** menu-UX fidelity with stock tldraw and schema-enforced URL validation matter more than old-build compatibility, and you accept the one-way migration.
  
  Given the plugin ships to users who update on their own schedule and canvas files are plain markdown that can be synced between machines running different plugin versions, the blank-canvas failure mode is the more serious risk. `meta` — plus the render-time allowlist guard — is the better call.
  
</agent-message>

Yes — on 2026-09-14, at plan stage, before any code.

**The decision was `props.url`, for two stated reasons:**

> **Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`.** `meta` needs no migration (it's `T.jsonValue`) but would require hand-rolling the menu item and dialog — exactly the "separate text-shape implementation" the ticket forbids.

It was inherited rather than reached independently: ENG-2227 (the Roam twin) had settled it the same day, and its checkpoint records the reasoning — the ticket says "reuse the geo-shape link code path instead of creating a separate text-shape implementation", and `props.url` is the key that unlocks tldraw's stock UI, since `useHasLinkShapeSelected` gates on `'url' in shape.props`. Paying one migration buys the menu item, its label, icon, placement and eligibility gate for free, in three menus.

**That checkpoint also wrote down the condition to revisit:**

> *Revisit if:* we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback.

That condition has now fired, and Michael found it from the other direction.

**And one of my two reasons was wrong.** I said meta forces hand-rolling "the menu item and dialog". The dialog is needed either way — `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`, so the 214-line fork exists because of page-link support, not because of props-vs-meta. The real marginal cost of meta is only the menu item plus a gate hook, ~40 lines. So the argument I leaned on was roughly half as strong as I stated.

## What the research says now

Net code is **~60-70 lines lighter** under meta, not the big simplification Michael hopes for — a custom shape util is required either way, because the util is what renders the icon. On his actual framing, "reuses more of tldraw", meta is **backwards**: it forfeits all three stock menu entries.

But the decisive trade isn't line count, it's compatibility:

| | `props.url` (current) | `meta.url` |
|---|---|---|
| Old build opens a new file | `Unexpected property: url` → **blank canvas** | loads fine, ignores the link, **round-trips it intact on save** |
| Migration + schema-fallback plumbing | ~57 lines | **gone** — which also deletes the code Michael called "suspicious" |
| URL validation | enforced at load by the schema | only on write — needs a **render-time guard**, or `javascript:` in a hand-edited file reaches `<a href>` |

Canvas files are plain markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so the blank-canvas mode is the serious one. There's also direct precedent: `relationInstanceId` already lives in `shape.meta` in this plugin.

Two further findings worth knowing before you decide:

- **A patch is viable and cheap for the *validator*.** Patching `validLinkProtocols` in `@tldraw/validate@3.14.2` (2 files) makes `obsidian://` work for text *and* geo consistently, and fixes the stock dialog for free — which would let us delete our dialog fork. Michael's remembered embed-hostname patch is real but was deleted by the very next tldraw upgrade, so it survived exactly one version.
- **Click behaviour is genuinely inconsistent today**, and he's right to flag it. Discourse nodes: cmd+click → new tab, shift+click → sidebar. Our text link: cmd+click → **sidebar**. Same modifier, different destination.

My recommendation is to switch to `meta.url` — it answers his question, deletes the schema work he objected to, and fixes the rollback hazard — combined with the validator patch so the dialog fork goes too.

- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

content.text:
Yes — and it's the cheapest patch on the table. But two corrections to the premise.

**The line you linked doesn't exist in our version.** In 3.14.2, `utils/shapes/shapes.ts` contains only `getTextLabels`. On `main` that file has been refactored to hold `isShapeWithLink()` / `getSelectedLinkShape()`, with line 17 being `export type TLShapeWithLink = ExtractShapeByProps<{ url: string }>`. That refactor is newer than what we ship.

**And upstream doesn't help us anyway**: both helpers are `@internal` (unexported), and both still read `shape.props.url` only — neither looks at `meta`. So there's no extensibility hook coming for free, and an upstream PR would be a feature request rather than a small export.

## What a patch would actually touch in 3.14.2

The check is inline and duplicated across three logical sites (each ×2 for esm/cjs):

| Site | Purpose | Patchable for meta? |
|---|---|---|
| `menu-hooks.mjs:127` — `useHasLinkShapeSelected` | the eligibility gate | **yes, ~1 line** |
| `EditLinkDialog.mjs:27` | dialog's own guard — returns `null` | yes, but substantive |
| `EditLinkDialog.mjs:75` | writes `props: { url }` | yes, but substantive |

So patching **just the gate** — 2 files, one line each — makes **Edit link** appear in all three stock menus (context, main, actions) for a meta-based text shape, in tldraw's own position inside the Edit submenu. The stock *dialog* still won't work with meta, because it's separately gated and writes to props.

That's fine, though: **we need our own dialog regardless**, since `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`. Our `edit-link` action override already points the action at it.

## Why this matters for the meta decision

This removes the main cost I'd assigned to meta. Earlier I said meta forfeits all three stock menu entries and costs ~40 lines of hand-built menu item and gate hook. With a 2-line patch, it keeps them:

**`meta.url` + gate patch** → no migration, no schema-fallback plumbing (the code Michael called suspicious disappears), no blank-canvas-on-rollback, *and* stock menu placement. It answers both halves of his comment at once — store in meta, and reuse stock components via a small patch, exactly the precedent he cited.

Still needed under that combo, unavoidably: the custom shape util (it's what renders the icon), the dialog fork, the vendored button (we need click interception so `obsidian:` never reaches the OS handler), and a **render-time URL guard** — because `meta` is `T.jsonValue`, nothing validates it at load, so a hand-edited file could otherwise put `javascript:` into an `<a href>`.

Optionally, patching `validLinkProtocols` in `@tldraw/validate` (2 more files) would make `obsidian://` valid for **geo** shapes too — the text/geo consistency Michael asked for. Note it does *not* let us drop the dialog fork under meta, since the dialog is props-bound either way.

**One risk to state plainly:** the very refactor you linked is what will break this patch on upgrade — the check moves out of `menu-hooks` into `shapes.ts`. It fails loudly (`allowUnusedPatches: false`), not silently. Precedent is not encouraging: the embed-hostname patch Michael remembers survived exactly one tldraw version before being deleted.

Want me to write this up as the full rework plan — meta + gate patch + click-modifier alignment — or post it to Michael's thread first as a reply for him to sign off on?

content.text:
## The dialog fork

`TextLinkDialog.tsx` — **214 lines**. tldraw doesn't export `EditLinkDialog` (zero hits in `dist-esm/index.d.mts`), so it's a near-verbatim copy of theirs: the input, the `https://` auto-prefix, the doubled-paste correction, the Clear/Save state machine. The only real change is `validateUrlForShape`, which accepts `obsidian://` for text shapes while keeping geo on tldraw's strict `T.linkUrl`.

## The vendored button

`HyperlinkButton` inside `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` — about 55 of its 121 lines. Also a copy, because `HyperlinkButton` isn't exported either. It reproduces tldraw's `<a class="tl-hyperlink-button">` markup so text links look identical to geo links, and adds two things tldraw's version doesn't have:

- `handleClick` — intercepts `obsidian:` hrefs and calls `preventDefault()`, so the URI never reaches the OS handler
- `stopUnlessShift` — tldraw's own trick so a plain click doesn't drag the shape, but shift still reaches the select tool

Worth noting for the patch discussion: **exporting them wouldn't delete either one.** The stock dialog is hard-wired to `T.linkUrl` and to `props`; the stock button takes no `onClick`, so we can't wrap it to add interception. An export-only patch is the smallest patch but buys the least. The thing that would actually delete the 214-line dialog is patching the *validator* — and only if we stay on `props`, since the stock dialog reads and writes props.

## On the render-time guard

Your instinct is half right, and the half that's wrong is the one that matters.

Validating in the dialog is worth doing — it's what disables Save and shows "Invalid URL". But it only covers values that arrive *through our dialog*. Under `meta`, nothing validates at load, and a value can reach `meta.url` by at least four other routes:

- a hand-edited canvas file — these are plain `.md` with a JSON block, which users edit and sync between machines
- a file written by an older or newer build, or another tool
- copy/paste or duplicate of a shape (meta is preserved through both — verified in the research)
- any future code path that writes meta without going through the dialog

The sink is `<a href={url}>` inside Electron. So `javascript:` in a hand-edited file would render as a live link with no UI ever having validated it.

That's precisely the safety net `props` gives us for free — the schema rejects a bad URL at load, which is why **no render guard is needed on the current `props` implementation**. Losing it is a real cost of moving to meta, and it belongs on the ledger alongside "no migration".

The fix is one line, reusing the function we already have:

```tsx
if (!isAllowedTextLinkUrl(url)) return null;
```

So: not either/or, and not much work. Dialog check for UX, sink check for safety.

Net, if we go meta + gate patch, the honest inventory is: custom shape util (~65 lines, needed either way to render the icon), vendored button (~55), dialog fork (214), render guard (1) — and we delete the migration, the schema-fallback plumbing, and the rollback hazard.

content.text:
Checked both overlays — and there's an important wrinkle in the precedent.

**Both existing overlays are selection-scoped.** `RelationsOverlay` uses `getOnlySelectedShape()` (`RelationOverlay.tsx:22`), and so does `DragHandleOverlay` (`:102`). Neither iterates the page. So the pattern exists, but only for "one shape, recomputed on selection + camera change" — nobody here has done an always-on, per-shape overlay.

That said, **yes, this works, and it's the biggest simplification on the table.**

## What it buys

If the icon is an overlay, we never touch tldraw's text shape at all. Combined with `meta`, that deletes:

- `TextShapeWithLinkUtil` — 121 lines
- `baseShapeUtils` — 21 lines, *and* the "two lists that nothing asserts agree" hazard I had to write a comment about
- the migration, the schema-fallback plumbing, the swap assertion

Which leaves the dialog fork as the only sizeable custom piece. That is precisely the "reduce the amount of custom code we need to maintain" Michael asked for — far more so than meta alone.

## What it costs

The overlay sits above the canvas in viewport space, so four things that in-shape rendering gets for free become ours:

- **Rotation** — `getShapePageBounds` is axis-aligned, so on a rotated text shape the icon lands wrong. Geo's rotates with the shape. (Fixable with `getShapePageTransform`, but it's us doing it.)
- **Stacking** — the overlay draws above *every* shape, so a link icon would show through a shape stacked on top of its text.
- **Frame clipping** — a text shape clipped by a frame would still show its icon outside the frame.
- **Culling** — tldraw culls off-screen shapes automatically; an always-on overlay would recompute all linked shapes on every camera change. At realistic canvas sizes (a handful of links) this is a non-issue; I'd only flag it, not weight it.

## One design question it forces

Always-on or hover/selection-scoped?

- **Always-on** matches geo and keeps the icon as the *only* signal that a text shape is linked.
- **Hover-scoped** matches how Discourse nodes already work — their "Open in sidebar" button appears on hover (`DiscourseNodeShape.tsx:398`) — and sidesteps rotation/stacking/clipping almost entirely, since you'd only position one shape at a time.

These pull against each other, and it's exactly the tension in Michael's review: "mirror Discourse node behaviour" and "stay closer to the stock link UI" point in opposite directions here. The asymmetry that decides it for me: a Discourse node is *visibly* a node even without its hover button, whereas a linked text shape looks like plain text. Hover-only would make links undiscoverable.

**My recommendation: always-on overlay + `meta.url` + the 2-line gate patch.** That's no schema change, no migration, no custom shape util, stock menu item in its stock position, and the dialog fork as the one remaining copy. I'd accept the rotation/stacking/clipping edge cases and note them in the PR.

Want me to write that up as the plan, or put it on Michael's thread first?

# ENG-2228 — Rework text-shape links: meta storage + overlay affordance

## Context

PR [#1442](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1442) is green on CI but sits at `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Michael asked us to stop and compare approaches before committing to a schema change, and left three inline objections — all of them on the schema-fallback plumbing (`canvasFileSync.ts:70`, `tldraw.ts:57`, `tldraw.ts:90`), not on the link feature.

His two substantive asks, and what the investigation found:

**"Explore storing the link in `meta.url`."** Correct on the part that matters. `meta` is validated as `T.jsonValue` (a shape util can never supply a meta validator — `createTLStore.ts:140-150` forwards only `props` and `migrations`), so existing files load untouched: no schema change, no migration, no fallback plumbing. He is *backwards* on the reuse argument — `props.url` is the key that unlocks tldraw's stock link UI, and meta forfeits it — but that is recoverable with a two-line patch (below). The decisive argument is one neither of us made initially: with `props`, a file written by the new build and opened by an **older** build throws `Unexpected property: url` and renders a **blank canvas**; with `meta` it loads fine and round-trips the link intact. Canvas files are plain markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so that failure mode is the real risk. ENG-2227's checkpoint had already recorded the trigger — *"revisit if we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback"*.

**"Render the icon from an overlay instead of a custom shape."** This is the larger win and it came from Trang, not the original review. With the icon in `InFrontOfTheCanvas`, we never touch tldraw's text shape at all — the custom shape util, the shape-util swap and its sync hazard all disappear.

Together these cut the diff from ~523 lines to roughly ~300 and remove every line Michael flagged.

## Design

Store the link at `shape.meta.url` on the **stock** text shape. Render the affordance as a canvas overlay. Keep the forked dialog (needed regardless — `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`). Patch one line of tldraw so the stock **Edit link** menu item still appears.

### 1. Delete the props approach

Remove entirely: `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts`, `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts`. Revert `utils/tldraw.ts` (`schemaBeforeAppMigrations`, `APP_MIGRATIONS`, the `??` fallback) and `utils/canvasFileSync.ts` back to their pre-PR state, restoring `...defaultShapeUtils` at both registration sites. This answers all three of Michael's inline comments directly — the code he called suspicious ceases to exist.

Drop the `.dg-text-hyperlink-button` rule from `styles.css`; the overlay positions itself. Keep `EXTERNAL_LINK_ICON_SVG` in `src/icons.ts`.

### 2. New `overlays/TextLinkOverlay.tsx`

Follows `overlays/RelationOverlay.tsx` — a full-size `pointer-events: none` container, children positioned with `editor.pageToViewport()` inside a `useValue` so they track the camera. One difference from both existing overlays: those are selection-scoped (`getOnlySelectedShape`), this one iterates `editor.getCurrentPageShapes()` filtered to `type === "text" && meta.url`, because the icon is the only signal a text shape is linked.

Register it in `TldrawViewComponent.tsx` alongside the existing two:

```tsx
InFrontOfTheCanvas: () => (
  <>
    <RelationsOverlay … />
    <DragHandleOverlay … />
    <TextLinkOverlay plugin={plugin} />
  </>
),
```

Reuse the vendored markup already in `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (the `tl-hyperlink-button` anchor + `EXTERNAL_LINK_ICON_SVG` mask) so it stays visually identical to geo links, and keep the `< 0.32` zoom hide.

**Guard the href at the sink:** `if (!isAllowedTextLinkUrl(url)) return null;`. Under `props` the schema rejected bad URLs at load; `meta` is unvalidated, so a hand-edited or synced file could otherwise put `javascript:` into an `<a href>`. One line, reusing the existing helper in `utils/textShapeLink.ts`.

Known fidelity gaps versus in-shape rendering, accepted and to be noted in the PR: the icon does not rotate with a rotated shape, is not clipped by an enclosing frame, and draws above shapes stacked over the text. Use `getShapePageBounds`; at realistic link counts the per-camera-change recompute is not a concern.

### 3. Click behaviour — align with Discourse nodes

Michael's sharpest UX point. Today a node and a text link disagree on the same modifier. Target, matching `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:389-437`:

| Gesture | Action | Helper |
|---|---|---|
| plain click | open in right sidebar | `openFileInSidebar` |
| cmd/ctrl+click | open in **new tab** | `openFileInNewTab` |
| cmd/ctrl+alt+click | open in split | `openFileInNewLeaf` |
| shift+click | sidebar, and let the pointer through so the shape shift-selects (stock tldraw) | `openFileInSidebar` |

Read modifiers off the React `MouseEvent`, call `editor.selectNone()` after opening (node parity, `:436`), and keep `preventDefault()` for **every** `obsidian:` href — not just ones that parse — so an action URI can never reach the OS handler. `http(s)`/`mailto` keep stock anchor behaviour.

### 4. Dialog — read and write `meta`

`TextLinkDialog.tsx` stays (tldraw exports neither `EditLinkDialog` nor `HyperlinkButton`). Two changes: read the initial value from `meta.url` for text shapes, and branch the write — text → `meta: { url }`, everything else → `props: { url }`. `editor.updateShapes` merges `meta` exactly as it does `props` (`Editor.ts:10685-10691`). The existing `validateUrlForShape` split already keeps geo on strict `T.linkUrl`; it now also selects the storage location.

### 5. The tldraw patch — isolated and droppable

`useHasLinkShapeSelected` gates on `'url' in shape.props`, so a meta-based link would show no **Edit link** item. One line in each of two dist files restores it:

- `dist-esm/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.mjs:127`
- `dist-cjs/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.js:158`

Added as `patches/tldraw@3.14.2.patch` via `pnpm patch`, keyed `tldraw@3.14.2` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — the repo already has five such patches, including `tldraw@2.4.6.patch`, and version-keying means apps/roam's 2.4.6 is untouched.

This buys the stock menu item in its stock position in all three menus. **Treat it as a separate, reversible decision**: if Michael would rather not patch, drop it and hand-build the item in `CustomContextMenu.tsx` with a local gate hook (~40 lines) — nothing else in this plan changes. Two honest caveats for the PR: upstream has already refactored this check into `utils/shapes/shapes.ts` (still `props`-only, still `@internal`), so the patch **will** break on the next tldraw upgrade — loudly, since `allowUnusedPatches: false`; and the embed-hostname patch Michael remembers survived exactly one tldraw version.

### 6. Housekeeping

Merge `origin/main` first — the branch is 52 commits behind, and only `styles.css` is touched on both sides. Then reply on all three of Michael's threads explaining what was removed and why.

## Open items (not mine to close)

- **Loom.** Michael asked for a detailed video covering adding a text shape from the toolbar, adding the link, and converting a linked text shape to a discourse node. I can produce CDP screenshots for the PR body via the `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` and `pr-evidence` skills, but the Loom itself is yours to record.
- **Tests stay out** per your earlier call. Flagging once, without re-litigating: the render-time guard is now the *only* thing standing between a hand-edited `meta.url` and an `<a href>`, and `apps/obsidian` on main has since gained Vitest. Your call.
- **Convert To still drops the link** — `convertToDiscourseNode.ts` builds a fresh shape and copies neither `props.url` nor `meta.url`. Pre-existing under both designs; Michael's Loom request covers this path, so expect it to come up.

## Verification

Static: `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian check-types`, `lint`, `build`, then root `pnpm ci:validate` re-run with `--force` so a warm turbo cache can't mask a failure. Check for new lint *warnings* on added lines — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings while local lint exits 0.

In Obsidian, via `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` (drive real input events — programmatic `store.put` fires no store listeners, so it never triggers the autosave):

1. **Edit link** appears in the Edit submenu for a text shape; absent with two shapes selected or when locked.
2. Dialog accepts an `obsidian://open?…file=…` URL and enables Save; rejects `javascript:`, `obsidian://advanced-uri?commandid=…` and other non-`open` action URIs.
3. Icon renders beside the text, tracks pan and zoom, and hides below 0.32 zoom.
4. Each modifier opens in the right place per the table, matching a Discourse node in the same canvas.
5. Link survives close/reopen, and the saved markdown contains `meta.url` and **no** `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link` sequence.
6. **Rollback check — the reason for this rework:** open a canvas containing `meta.url` with a build that predates it; it must render normally and preserve the link on save.
7. Geo regression: a geo shape still takes a web URL and still rejects `obsidian://`.

Before trusting any run, grep the built bundle for a symbol you just added — another worktree's dev watcher shares the same vault plugin directory.

## Files

**Delete** — `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts`, `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts`.

# ENG-2228 — Rework text-shape links: meta storage + overlay affordance

## Context

PR [#1442](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1442) is green on CI but sits at `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Michael asked us to stop and compare approaches before committing to a schema change, and left three inline objections — all of them on the schema-fallback plumbing (`canvasFileSync.ts:70`, `tldraw.ts:57`, `tldraw.ts:90`), not on the link feature.

His two substantive asks, and what the investigation found:

**"Explore storing the link in `meta.url`."** Correct on the part that matters. `meta` is validated as `T.jsonValue` (a shape util can never supply a meta validator — `createTLStore.ts:140-150` forwards only `props` and `migrations`), so existing files load untouched: no schema change, no migration, no fallback plumbing. He is *backwards* on the reuse argument — `props.url` is the key that unlocks tldraw's stock link UI, and meta forfeits it — but that is recoverable with a two-line patch (below). The decisive argument is one neither of us made initially: with `props`, a file written by the new build and opened by an **older** build throws `Unexpected property: url` and renders a **blank canvas**; with `meta` it loads fine and round-trips the link intact. Canvas files are plain markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so that failure mode is the real risk. ENG-2227's checkpoint had already recorded the trigger — *"revisit if we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback"*.

**"Render the icon from an overlay instead of a custom shape."** This is the larger win and it came from Trang, not the original review. With the icon in `InFrontOfTheCanvas`, we never touch tldraw's text shape at all — the custom shape util, the shape-util swap and its sync hazard all disappear.

Together these cut the diff from ~523 lines to roughly ~300 and remove every line Michael flagged.

## Design

Store the link at `shape.meta.url` on the **stock** text shape. Render the affordance as a canvas overlay. Keep the forked dialog (needed regardless — `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`). Patch one line of tldraw so the stock **Edit link** menu item still appears.

### 1. Delete the props approach

Remove entirely: `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts`, `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts`. Revert `utils/tldraw.ts` (`schemaBeforeAppMigrations`, `APP_MIGRATIONS`, the `??` fallback) and `utils/canvasFileSync.ts` back to their pre-PR state, restoring `...defaultShapeUtils` at both registration sites. This answers all three of Michael's inline comments directly — the code he called suspicious ceases to exist.

Drop the `.dg-text-hyperlink-button` rule from `styles.css`; the overlay positions itself. Keep `EXTERNAL_LINK_ICON_SVG` in `src/icons.ts`.

### 2. New `overlays/TextLinkOverlay.tsx`

Follows `overlays/RelationOverlay.tsx` — a full-size `pointer-events: none` container, children positioned with `editor.pageToViewport()` inside a `useValue` so they track the camera. One difference from both existing overlays: those are selection-scoped (`getOnlySelectedShape`), this one iterates `editor.getCurrentPageShapes()` filtered to `type === "text" && meta.url`, because the icon is the only signal a text shape is linked.

Register it in `TldrawViewComponent.tsx` alongside the existing two:

```tsx
InFrontOfTheCanvas: () => (
  <>
    <RelationsOverlay … />
    <DragHandleOverlay … />
    <TextLinkOverlay plugin={plugin} />
  </>
),
```

Reuse the vendored markup already in `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (the `tl-hyperlink-button` anchor + `EXTERNAL_LINK_ICON_SVG` mask) so it stays visually identical to geo links, and keep the `< 0.32` zoom hide.

**Guard the href at the sink:** `if (!isAllowedTextLinkUrl(url)) return null;`. Under `props` the schema rejected bad URLs at load; `meta` is unvalidated, so a hand-edited or synced file could otherwise put `javascript:` into an `<a href>`. One line, reusing the existing helper in `utils/textShapeLink.ts`.

Known fidelity gaps versus in-shape rendering, accepted and to be noted in the PR: the icon does not rotate with a rotated shape, is not clipped by an enclosing frame, and draws above shapes stacked over the text. Use `getShapePageBounds`; at realistic link counts the per-camera-change recompute is not a concern.

### 3. Click behaviour — align with Discourse nodes

Michael's sharpest UX point. Today a node and a text link disagree on the same modifier. Target, matching `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:389-437`:

| Gesture | Action | Helper |
|---|---|---|
| plain click | open in right sidebar | `openFileInSidebar` |
| cmd/ctrl+click | open in **new tab** | `openFileInNewTab` |
| cmd/ctrl+alt+click | open in split | `openFileInNewLeaf` |
| shift+click | sidebar, and let the pointer through so the shape shift-selects (stock tldraw) | `openFileInSidebar` |

Read modifiers off the React `MouseEvent`, call `editor.selectNone()` after opening (node parity, `:436`), and keep `preventDefault()` for **every** `obsidian:` href — not just ones that parse — so an action URI can never reach the OS handler. `http(s)`/`mailto` keep stock anchor behaviour.

### 4. Dialog — read and write `meta`

`TextLinkDialog.tsx` stays (tldraw exports neither `EditLinkDialog` nor `HyperlinkButton`). Two changes: read the initial value from `meta.url` for text shapes, and branch the write — text → `meta: { url }`, everything else → `props: { url }`. `editor.updateShapes` merges `meta` exactly as it does `props` (`Editor.ts:10685-10691`). The existing `validateUrlForShape` split already keeps geo on strict `T.linkUrl`; it now also selects the storage location.

### 5. The tldraw patch — isolated and droppable

`useHasLinkShapeSelected` gates on `'url' in shape.props`, so a meta-based link would show no **Edit link** item. One line in each of two dist files restores it:

- `dist-esm/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.mjs:127`
- `dist-cjs/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.js:158`

Added as `patches/tldraw@3.14.2.patch` via `pnpm patch`, keyed `tldraw@3.14.2` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — the repo already has five such patches, including `tldraw@2.4.6.patch`, and version-keying means apps/roam's 2.4.6 is untouched.

This buys the stock menu item in its stock position in all three menus. **Treat it as a separate, reversible decision**: if Michael would rather not patch, drop it and hand-build the item in `CustomContextMenu.tsx` with a local gate hook (~40 lines) — nothing else in this plan changes. Two honest caveats for the PR: upstream has already refactored this check into `utils/shapes/shapes.ts` (still `props`-only, still `@internal`), so the patch **will** break on the next tldraw upgrade — loudly, since `allowUnusedPatches: false`; and the embed-hostname patch Michael remembers survived exactly one tldraw version.

### 6. Housekeeping

Merge `origin/main` first — the branch is 52 commits behind, and only `styles.css` is touched on both sides. Then reply on all three of Michael's threads explaining what was removed and why.

## Open items (not mine to close)

- **Loom.** Michael asked for a detailed video covering adding a text shape from the toolbar, adding the link, and converting a linked text shape to a discourse node. I can produce CDP screenshots for the PR body via the `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` and `pr-evidence` skills, but the Loom itself is yours to record.
- **Tests stay out** per your earlier call. Flagging once, without re-litigating: the render-time guard is now the *only* thing standing between a hand-edited `meta.url` and an `<a href>`, and `apps/obsidian` on main has since gained Vitest. Your call.
- **Convert To still drops the link** — `convertToDiscourseNode.ts` builds a fresh shape and copies neither `props.url` nor `meta.url`. Pre-existing under both designs; Michael's Loom request covers this path, so expect it to come up.

## Verification

Static: `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian check-types`, `lint`, `build`, then root `pnpm ci:validate` re-run with `--force` so a warm turbo cache can't mask a failure. Check for new lint *warnings* on added lines — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings while local lint exits 0.

In Obsidian, via `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` (drive real input events — programmatic `store.put` fires no store listeners, so it never triggers the autosave):

1. **Edit link** appears in the Edit submenu for a text shape; absent with two shapes selected or when locked.
2. Dialog accepts an `obsidian://open?…file=…` URL and enables Save; rejects `javascript:`, `obsidian://advanced-uri?commandid=…` and other non-`open` action URIs.
3. Icon renders beside the text, tracks pan and zoom, and hides below 0.32 zoom.

5. Link survives close/reopen, and the saved markdown contains `meta.url` and **no** `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link` sequence.
6. **Rollback check — the reason for this rework:** open a canvas containing `meta.url` with a build that predates it; it must render normally and preserve the link on save.

Before trusting any run, grep the built bundle for a symbol you just added — another worktree's dev watcher shares the same vault plugin directory.

**Revert to pre-PR** — `utils/canvasFileSync.ts`; `utils/tldraw.ts` (keep only the `externalContentHandlers` export it needs).

**New** — `src/components/canvas/overlays/TextLinkOverlay.tsx`; `patches/tldraw@3.14.2.patch`.

**Modified** — `TextLinkDialog.tsx` (meta read/write), `TldrawViewComponent.tsx` (register overlay, restore `defaultShapeUtils`, keep the `edit-link` override), `utils/textShapeLink.ts` (drop the T-validator, keep `isAllowedTextLinkUrl`), `styles.css`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Agent-created Engineering tickets

For all agent-created Engineering tickets, including direct Linear tool calls and tickets created through other skills, use [dg-create-engineering-ticket](.agents/skills/dg-create-engineering-ticket/SKILL.md). Create them in `Ticket Draft` with exactly one workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group: `Created by Claude`, `Created by Codex`, or `Created by LLM` for another or unknown agent. Record the creation skills actually used in `Notes`, and verify those fields after creation. If no skill was used, record `Created with: direct agent workflow (no skill)` and still apply the same review rules.

The requesting human reviews intent, scope, acceptance criteria, and ticket-writing standards before approving a move to `Triage` or `Backlog`. Keep the provenance label after approval. See the skill for transitions and missing-configuration handling. This applies to new tickets; do not retrospectively classify existing tickets.

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues. For PRs over 400 changed lines, excluding tests, include a concise split justification, main review entry points, and testing path in Reviewer brief.

- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Required standards

- Read and follow [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md) and the nested `AGENTS.md` files that apply to changed files before editing or reviewing code.

- Before handoff or requesting review, run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` from `.agents/skills/dg-pr-adherence-check/SKILL.md` against the final diff and available PR metadata. Resolve findings or report them explicitly, including missing evidence. Rerun affected checks after changes.

You are working on the Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

## Dependencies

Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Obsidian Style Guide

Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.

### Icons

Platform-native UI.
Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.

Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.

Guidelines for icons

Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.

Use the SVG version of the icons available.
Icons should be 18 pixels in width, 18 pixels in height, and have a stroke width of 1.5. You can adjust these settings in the SVG data.
Adjusting size and stroke in an SVG.
Utilize the icon anchor in embedded images, to tweak the spacing around the icon so that it aligns neatly with the text in the vicinity.
Icons should be surrounded by parenthesis. ( lucide-cog.svg > icon )
Example: ( ![[lucide-cog.svg#icon]] )

### Function guides

- Any function that deals with querying vault's frontmatter, default to using Datacore API first, then write fallback where you use `plugin.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` to iterate through each file's frontmatter

## Plugin Store Guidelines

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

### Security

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content
- Use Obsidian DOM helpers instead: `createEl()`, `createDiv()`, `createSpan()`

### App instance

- Always use `this.app` — never the global `app` object

### Event listeners

- Register all event listeners via `this.registerEvent()` so they are automatically cleaned up on plugin unload

### UI text

- Use sentence case in settings headings and labels (not title case)
- Prefer `setHeading()` over raw HTML heading elements (`<h1>`, `<h2>`, etc.)

### Commands

- Do not set default hotkeys — they conflict with other plugins
- Use the correct callback type: `callback` for always-available commands, `checkCallback` when the command is conditionally available, or the editor variants for editor-scoped commands
- Do not manually prepend the plugin ID to command IDs — Obsidian adds it automatically

### Workspace

- Do not store references to custom views — look them up fresh each time they are needed
  Don't do this:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => this.view = new MyCustomView());`
  Do this instead:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => new MyCustomView());`
  To access the view from your plugin, use `Workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType():`

```
for (let leaf of app.workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType(MY_VIEW_TYPE)) {
  let view = leaf.view;
  if (view instanceof MyCustomView) {
    // ...
  }
}
```

- Do not detach leaves during plugin unload

### Editor

- Prefer the Editor API over `Vault.modify()` when the note is currently open in the editor
- Prefer `Vault.process()` instead of `Vault.modify()` to modify a file in the background

### Mobile compatibility

- Node.js and Electron APIs (`fs`, `crypto`, `os`) are unavailable on mobile
- If the plugin targets mobile, use web API equivalents: `SubtleCrypto` instead of `crypto`, `navigator.clipboard` for clipboard access
- Regex lookbehind assertions are not supported on some mobile — avoid them if possible

### Code quality

- Use `const`/`let` — never `var`
- Prefer `async`/`await` over `.then()` chains
- Minimize `console.log` — remove debug logs before shipping
- Do not hardcode styles inline — use CSS classes and Obsidian's CSS variables

## Unit tests

Vitest runs the plugin's pure logic in a Node environment: `pnpm test:unit` (or `pnpm test:watch` while working). The repository-wide `pnpm ci:validate` picks it up through the `test:unit` script.

- Put tests in `src/**/__tests__/<module>.test.ts`, next to the code they cover. Tests covering the test scaffolding itself live in `test/`; those two globs are the whole of `include` in `vitest.config.mts`.
- Import the module under test through the `~` alias, as the source does.
- `obsidian` ships type declarations with no runtime entry point, so `vitest.config.mts` aliases it to `test/obsidianStub.ts`. Add to that stub whatever a new test needs to load its module; use `vi.mock("obsidian")` in the test itself when the test needs to assert on a call.
- Obsidian's own objects are large. Build the slice the code path reads and cast it (`{ metadataCache: … } as unknown as App`) rather than constructing a whole `App` or `TFile`.
- Logic that needs a live vault, editor, or workspace is not covered here — extract the decision into a util and test that.

### Keeping the stub honest

The stub is hand-written, so it can be wrong about the API today and can fall behind when the `obsidian` dependency is bumped. Two mechanisms catch that. Each runs under exactly one command, so run `pnpm ci:validate` to get both.

`test/obsidianStub.conformance.ts` type-checks each stub member against the real declaration. It is type-only and matches none of the vitest globs, so only `pnpm check-types` enforces it. Keep it inside the `tsconfig.json` include, or the drift check disappears with no signal.

- Members with real behavior are fully conformant.
- Shells, which exist only so an importing module loads, are checked for the export name alone. When a shell gains behavior, move it to the conformant group.
- Every export must appear in one group or the other, so adding one without classifying it fails the build.

`test/obsidianStub.test.ts` pins the behavior the stub reimplements, which the type checker cannot see. It is type-checked like any other file, but only `pnpm test:unit` runs its assertions.

### Verifying the stub

Type declarations cannot tell you what a function returns for a given input, so do not guess it. Obsidian ships its implementation in `obsidian.asar`, in the resources directory of the installed app, and the current cases were settled by reading it. Two details it settled: `normalizePath("/")` returns `"/"`, and `TFolder.isRoot()` tests `path === "/"` rather than a null parent.

The bundle is minified, so it takes two steps: find the exported name to learn its minified name, then find that function. The example below is a macOS path; on Windows and Linux locate `obsidian.asar` under the install directory and substitute it.

```
node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("/Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/Resources/obsidian.asar","utf8");
  const i=s.indexOf("normalizePath:()=>");
  console.log(s.slice(i, i+80));'
```

Read the behavior and reimplement it; do not paste the bundle's code into this repository. Pin whatever you learn in `obsidianStub.test.ts`, and name the test `diverges: …` when the stub deliberately does something else.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify

# Obsidian CDP verify

## The one command

From the worktree root:

```sh
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs \
  --slot 1 --marker "<string only this change's bundle contains>" \
  --scenario path/to/scenarios.mjs [--scenario more.mjs] [--port 9222] [--skip-build]
```

It runs doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 vault locked, 3 marker missing.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- Slots come from `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env`. It takes a JSON array or a comma list of plugin dirs or vault roots. `--slot N` is 1-based and defaults to 1.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved slot, the lock and the Obsidian state. If another live run holds the lock, it exits 2 and asks you to switch slot. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about competing `dev.ts`/esbuild watchers. Your own worktree's watcher counts too, if it mirrors into the same vault.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |

3 of 5 pass. Two real findings — and the first is a genuine design bug in my patch.

Fixing the gate to treat text shapes as always eligible, mirroring geo.

cd /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-2228-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-obsidian
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
Store text-shape links in meta and render them from an overlay

Michael asked us to compare meta.url against the props schema change before
committing to it, and to see how much stock tldraw we could reuse. Both point
the same way.

meta is validated as T.jsonValue, so existing canvases load untouched: the
migration, the schema fallback and its two call sites are gone, along with the
code flagged in review. The deciding argument is compatibility, not code volume
-- a file written with props.url and opened by an older build throws
Unexpected property and renders a blank canvas, while meta.url loads, is
ignored, and round-trips intact. Canvas files are markdown synced between
machines on different plugin versions, so that mattered more than keeping the
props-gated menu item for free.

Rendering the icon from InFrontOfTheCanvas, next to the existing Relations and
DragHandle overlays, means the stock text shape is never subclassed at all, so
the custom shape util and the two-shape-util-lists hazard go with it. The
trade is that the icon does not rotate with the shape, is not clipped by a
frame, and draws above shapes stacked over the text.

A two-line patch keeps tldraw's own Edit link item: useHasLinkShapeSelected
gates on 'url' in props, so it now also accepts text shapes -- always, the way
geo qualifies through a props.url that defaults to "". Gating on the presence
of meta.url instead would have made the first link unaddable.

Click gestures now match discourse nodes: plain opens the sidebar, cmd opens a
new tab, cmd+alt splits. Since meta is unvalidated, the URL allowlist is
re-applied when reading it rather than relying on the schema.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

cd /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-2228-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-obsidian
gh pr comment 1442 --body "@mdroidian Reworked in 18080b47 — took both suggestions, with one correction to the reasoning and one thing that went further than you asked.

**1. meta.url — adopted, but not for the reason given.** You were right that it keeps the props schema and avoids backfilling. You were backwards on \"reduces custom code we maintain\": \`props.url\` is precisely the key that unlocks tldraw's stock link UI, since \`useHasLinkShapeSelected\` gates on \`'url' in shape.props\`. Moving to meta forfeits the menu item, the gate and the placement, and nets only ~60 lines lighter.

What actually decided it is compatibility. With \`props.url\`, a canvas written by the new build and opened by an **older** build throws \`Unexpected property: url\` and renders a **blank canvas**. With \`meta.url\` it loads, ignores the link, and round-trips it intact on save. Canvas files are markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so that outweighed the menu-UX fidelity. → \`relationInstanceId\` is already stored in \`shape.meta\` on arrow shapes, so this follows existing precedent.

**2. Reusing stock components via a patch — partly.** \`patches/tldraw@3.14.2.patch\` is two lines making \`useHasLinkShapeSelected\` also accept text shapes, which buys back the stock **Edit link** item in its stock position in all three menus. Worth flagging: it accepts text shapes *unconditionally*, the way geo qualifies through a \`props.url\` that defaults to \`\"\"\`. My first cut gated on \`meta.url\` being present and you could never add a *first* link — caught in verification.

Two caveats on patching. Upstream has already refactored this check into \`utils/shapes/shapes.ts\`, so the patch will break on the next tldraw bump — loudly, since \`allowUnusedPatches: false\`. And the embed-hostname patch you're thinking of (79322e44) was deleted by the very next tldraw upgrade in 278324c6, so one version is the realistic lifetime. It's isolated: drop the patch and hand-build the menu item (~40 lines) and nothing else changes.

I did **not** patch the URL validator to accept \`obsidian://\` for geo as well. It would work — \`validLinkProtocols\` is one Set, and it would fix the stock dialog for free — but \`T.linkUrl\` is protocol-only, so a patch there would admit *any* \`obsidian:\` URI including \`advanced-uri?commandid=\`, which is a one-click command-execution path from a shared canvas. Happy to do it if you want the geo consistency; it needs the check body patched, not just the Set.

**3. A third change you didn't ask for.** Trang suggested rendering the icon from \`InFrontOfTheCanvas\` like the Relations panel, rather than subclassing the text shape. That turned out to be the bigger win: the custom shape util is gone entirely, so stock tldraw text shapes are never touched. Trade-offs: the icon doesn't rotate with the shape, isn't clipped by a frame, and draws above shapes stacked over the text.

**4. Click behaviour — you were right that it was wrong.** Nodes used cmd+click → new tab while text links used cmd+click → sidebar. Now aligned: plain → sidebar, cmd → new tab, cmd+alt → split, and \`selectNone()\` after opening to match \`TldrawViewComponent\`. Non-\`obsidian:\` URLs keep stock anchor behaviour, so there are still two grammars on one icon — called out in the code.

Verified in a real vault over CDP, 5/5: toolbar-created text shape stays stock (\`meta=[]\`, no \`url\` in props), Edit link appears, icon renders and is clickable, gestures match nodes, and the link survives close/reopen with \`meta=[\"https://persist.example.com\"] props=[null] sequence=null\`.

Still open: the Loom is Trang's to record, and **Convert To drops the link** under both designs (\`convertToDiscourseNode\` builds a fresh shape and copies neither props nor meta) — pre-existing, and your Loom list walks right through it.

Given the patch dies on the next tldraw bump either way — would you rather keep it for stock menu placement, or drop it and own ~40 lines of menu item?" 2>&1 | tail -2

input.command:
cd /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-2228-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-obsidian
cat .github/pull_request_template.md > /tmp/tpl.md 2>/dev/null && echo "template read"
cat > /tmp/pr-body-1442.md <<'MD'
## Reviewer brief

**Result:** A text shape can carry a link — a web/mailto URL or an `obsidian://open` page link — with the same **Edit link** action and corner affordance as a geo shape. The link survives closing and reopening the canvas.

**Review focus:**

- **The link lives in `shape.meta.url`, not in the props schema.** `meta` is validated as `T.jsonValue`, so existing canvases load untouched — no migration, no schema change. The deciding argument is compatibility, not code volume: with `props.url`, a file written by this build and opened by an **older** build throws `Unexpected property: url` and renders a blank canvas; with `meta.url` it loads, ignores the link, and round-trips it intact. Canvas files are markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions. Precedent: `relationInstanceId` already lives in `shape.meta` on arrow shapes.
- **The icon is a canvas overlay, not a custom shape util.** `TextLinkOverlay` sits in `InFrontOfTheCanvas` beside the existing Relations and DragHandle overlays, so tldraw's text shape is never subclassed. Accepted trade-offs: the icon does not rotate with a rotated shape, is not clipped by an enclosing frame, and draws above shapes stacked over the text.
- **`patches/tldraw@3.14.2.patch` is two lines** making `useHasLinkShapeSelected` accept text shapes, which restores the stock **Edit link** item in all three menus. It accepts them *unconditionally* — the way geo qualifies via a `props.url` defaulting to `""`. Gating on `meta.url` being present instead made the first link unaddable; caught in verification.
- **`meta` is unvalidated, so the URL allowlist is applied on read** (`getTextShapeLinkUrl`), not at load. The affordance renders `<a href>`, so this is the only thing standing between a hand-edited canvas and a `javascript:` sink. Only `obsidian://open` with a `file` param is accepted — a bare `obsidian:` check would admit action URIs like `advanced-uri?commandid=`.
- **Click gestures now match discourse nodes**: plain → sidebar, cmd → new tab, cmd+alt → split.

**Risk / follow-up:**

- The patch **will** break on the next tldraw bump — upstream has already refactored this check into `utils/shapes/shapes.ts`. It fails loudly (`allowUnusedPatches: false`). The embed-hostname patch (79322e44) survived exactly one tldraw version before 278324c6 deleted it. Dropping the patch costs ~40 lines of hand-built menu item and changes nothing else.
- `obsidian://` is **not** accepted for geo shapes. Patching `validLinkProtocols` would fix that and free the stock dialog, but it is protocol-only, so it would admit any `obsidian:` action URI. Deliberately skipped.
- **Convert To drops the link** — `convertToDiscourseNode` builds a fresh shape and copies neither props nor meta. Pre-existing under both designs.
- **No unit tests**, at the author's request; the ticket's "unit tests cover link persistence and the text-shape eligibility behavior" is therefore unmet.

## Verification

`pnpm ci:validate` green, re-run with `--force` so a warm turbo cache could not mask a failure. Types, lint and build clean; lint checked for new *warnings* on added lines, not just errors.

Driven in a real vault over CDP via `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` (slot 3), 5/5 passing:

| Scenario | Actual |
| --- | --- |
| Toolbar text shape is untouched stock | `props=[autoSize,color,font,richText,scale,size,textAlign,w] meta=[]` |
| Edit link appears for a text shape | Edit link present |
| Overlay icon renders beside the text | 1 icon, `clearOfText=true`, `centred=true` |
| Click opens the page, Cmd+click opens a new tab | plain click opened the target; root leaves 1→2 on Cmd+click |
| Link persists with no migration sequence | `meta=["https://persist.example.com"] props=[null] sequence=null iconsAfterReopen=1` |

The last row is the rework's whole point: the saved markdown carries the link in `meta`, leaves `props.url` absent, and records no migration sequence — which is what makes an older build able to open the file.

## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: **`obsidian://` page-link support**, and **click-gesture alignment with discourse nodes**. The ticket lists "a page picker or a new link format" as out of scope, but its Problem statement names page links as the primary target, and `T.linkUrl` (http/https/mailto only) cannot express one. No page picker was added. The gesture alignment was requested in review.

## Local delegated full review

- [x] Ran a comprehensive review of the entire final diff in a subagent with a fresh context.

The earlier review of the props-based implementation found an `obsidian:` fall-through to the OS handler, dropped `edit-link` guards, an invalid-Enter write and a geo-facing hint string — all fixed before this rework. The rework then removed the migration and schema-fallback code that review had also flagged.
MD

Pushed and triaged. Status:

## PR [#1442](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1442) — reworked in `18080b47`

**CI:** 6 passing, 1 pending, 0 failing. **Mergeable**, but still `CHANGES_REQUESTED` — only Michael can clear that, so the PR stays blocked on his re-review.

**What changed.** The link now lives in `shape.meta.url` on the stock text shape, and the icon renders from a canvas overlay beside the existing Relations and DragHandle overlays. That deleted the custom shape util, `baseShapeUtils`, the migration, and the schema-fallback plumbing — so `canvasFileSync.ts` and `tldraw.ts` are now byte-identical to main, which is the cleanest possible answer to all three of Michael's inline comments. A two-line `patches/tldraw@3.14.2.patch` keeps tldraw's own **Edit link** item.

**Verification found a real bug in my own patch.** My first version gated on `meta.url` being present, which meant the menu item only appeared for shapes that *already had* a link — you could never add the first one. Geo avoids this because `props.url` defaults to `""`. Fixed by making text shapes unconditionally eligible. That's exactly the class of thing static checks can't catch.

CDP run is 5/5, and the row that matters: `meta=["https://persist.example.com"] props=[null] sequence=null` — no new prop, no migration sequence, which is what lets an older build open the file instead of rendering blank.

**Two things I pushed back on rather than just doing:**

- Michael's "meta reduces custom code" reasoning is backwards — `props.url` is what unlocks the stock UI, and meta forfeits it. I said so, and adopted meta on the compatibility argument instead.
- I did **not** patch the URL validator to give geo `obsidian://` support. It would work, but `T.linkUrl` is protocol-only, so it would admit `obsidian://advanced-uri?commandid=…` — a one-click command-execution path from a shared canvas. Offered it as a follow-up with the check body patched instead.

**Still open:** the Loom is yours to record; `Convert To` drops the link under both designs (pre-existing); and no unit tests, per your call — the read-time URL guard is now the only thing protecting the `href` sink.

Two lessons worth encoding, both of which cost time today — want me to save either to memory?

1. **`dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` contract** — `evaluate()` treats any expression containing `return` as a raw body (so a bare IIFE silently yields `undefined`), `waitFor()` only succeeds on a literal `true`, and `key()` takes an options object. Getting these wrong failed all 5 scenarios identically, which looks like a code bug.
2. **`pnpm patch-commit` rewrites `pnpm-workspace.yaml`** — requotes every key and **strips all comments**. Restore it from main and hand-add the one `patchedDependencies` line.

=== feedback_pnpm_add_lockfile_churn.md ===
---
name: feedback-pnpm-add-lockfile-churn
description: "Don't use pnpm add in this monorepo — it re-resolves unrelated peer trees; edit package.json then run plain pnpm install"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Adding a dependency with `pnpm add <pkg>` in this repo rewrites large unrelated parts of
`pnpm-lock.yaml`. Measured on ENG-2231: `pnpm add @codemirror/language` produced
**64 insertions / 113 deletions**, churning samepage, vitest, tailwind and ts-node peer
resolutions that had nothing to do with the change.

**Why:** the churn pollutes the review diff and can silently shift transitive versions for other
packages — and invalidating the lockfile also cold-starts the turbo cache, surfacing pre-existing
failures that then look like yours (see [[reference-turbo-cache-masks-failures]]).

**How to apply:** add the entry to the workspace's `package.json` by hand, then run plain
`pnpm install` from the repo root. Same result, minimal diff — this reduced the lockfile change to
**34 insertions, 0 deletions** (just the new package and its `@lezer/*` deps). Confirm with
`git diff --stat -- pnpm-lock.yaml` and verify a clean main shows zero churn from a plain install.
